title.zh: 卷一百三十六 列傳第二十三: 哈剌哈孫 阿沙不花 拜住
title.raw: 卷一百三十六 列傳第二十三: 哈剌哈孫 阿沙不花 拜住 Volume 136 Biographies 23: Halahasun, Ashabuhua, Baizhu

sentences.zh: 哈剌哈孫

translations.literal: Harqasun
translations.idiomatic: Harqasun

sentences.zh: 哈剌哈孫，斡剌納兒氏。

translations.literal: Harqasun, of the Oranar clan.
translations.idiomatic: Harqasun belonged to the Oranar clan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖啟昔禮，始事王可汗脫斡璘。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Qisili first served the Wang Khan Tuowohuan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Qisili had first entered the service of Wang Khan Tuowohuan.

sentences.zh: 王可汗與太祖約為兄弟，及太祖得衆，陰忌之，謀害太祖。

translations.literal: The Wang Khan and Taizu pledged brotherhood; when Taizu gained followers, he secretly envied him and plotted to harm Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Khan and Taizu had sworn brotherhood, but once Taizu gathered a following, Wang Khan secretly resented him and laid plans to kill him.

sentences.zh: 啟昔禮潛以其謀來告，太祖乃與二十餘人一夕遁去，諸部聞者多歸之，還攻滅王可汗，併其衆。

translations.literal: Qisili secretly came to report his plot; Taizu then fled in one night with more than twenty men; many tribes hearing of it joined him; he returned to attack and destroy the Wang Khan and annex his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Qisili secretly informed Taizu of the plot. Taizu fled overnight with a score of companions, and as word spread, many tribes rallied to him. He then turned back, destroyed Wang Khan, and absorbed his following.

sentences.zh: 擢啟昔禮為千戶，賜號荅剌罕。

translations.literal: Qisili was promoted to chiliarch and granted the title Darqan.
translations.idiomatic: Qisili was promoted to command of a thousand households and honored with the title Darqan.

sentences.zh: 從平河西、西域諸國。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Hexi and the various states of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned in the pacification of Hexi and the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 祖博理察，太宗時從太弟睿宗攻河南，取汴、蔡，滅金，賜順德以為分邑。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bolicha, in Taizong's time followed the Grand Imperial Younger Brother Ruizong in attacking Henan, took Bian and Cai, destroyed Jin, and was granted Shunde as his appanage.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bolicha, under Taizong, followed the Grand Imperial Younger Brother Ruizong in the assault on Henan, captured Bian and Cai, and helped bring down the Jin; Shunde was granted him as a fief.

sentences.zh: 父囊加台，從憲宗伐蜀，卒于軍。

translations.literal: His father Nangatai followed Möngke in campaigning against Shu and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Nangatai accompanied Möngke in the conquest of Shu and died on campaign.

sentences.zh: 哈剌哈孫威重，不妄言笑，善騎射，工國書，又雅重儒術。

translations.literal: Harqasun was august and grave; he did not speak or laugh lightly; he was skilled at mounted archery and adept at the national script, and also esteemed Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: Harqasun carried himself with grave dignity and rarely spoke or laughed lightly. He was an expert horseman and archer, proficient in the Mongol script, and held the Confucian tradition in high regard.

sentences.zh: 至元九年，世祖錄勳臣後，命掌宿衞，襲號答剌罕。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhiyuan, Shizu recorded the descendants of meritorious ministers and ordered him to take charge of the palace guard, inheriting the title Darqan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1272 Kublai reviewed the heirs of meritorious ministers, appointed him to command the palace guard, and confirmed his inheritance of the title Darqan.

sentences.zh: 自是人稱答剌罕而不名。

translations.literal: From then on people called him Darqan and not by his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he was known simply as Darqan rather than by his personal name.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗諭之曰：「汝家勳載王府，行且大用汝矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor once instructed him, saying: "Your family's merit is recorded in the princely house; before long I shall employ you on a grand scale."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told him, "Your family's service to the imperial house is recorded in merit rolls; I shall soon give you great responsibility."

sentences.zh: 又語皇太子曰：「荅剌罕非常人比，可善遇之。」

translations.literal: He also told the crown prince: "Darqan is not to be compared with ordinary men; you should treat him well."
translations.idiomatic: He also said to the crown prince, "Darqan is no ordinary man; treat him with respect."

sentences.zh: 十八年，割欽、廉二州，益其食邑。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Qin and Lian prefectures were carved out to augment his fief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1281 Qin and Lian were detached from other jurisdictions and added to his appanage.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，拜大宗正。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed Grand Judge of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1285 he was appointed Grand Judge of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 用法平允，審錄冤滯，所活數百人。

translations.literal: In applying the law he was fair and even-handed; in reviewing cases of wrongful imprisonment he saved several hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: He applied the law with evenhanded fairness, reviewed cases of wrongful imprisonment, and saved several hundred lives.

sentences.zh: 時相請以江南獄隸宗正。

translations.literal: At the time the chief minister requested that Jiangnan prisons be placed under the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the chief minister proposed placing all Jiangnan criminal cases under the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 哈剌哈孫曰：「江南新附，教令未孚，且相去數千里，欲遙制其刑獄，得無冤乎。」

translations.literal: Harqasun said: "Jiangnan has only recently submitted; imperial orders have not yet won full compliance, and it is moreover several thousand li distant—if we wish to control its criminal justice from afar, will there not be wrongful convictions?"
translations.idiomatic: Harqasun said, "Jiangnan has only just submitted; imperial orders have not yet taken firm hold there, and it lies thousands of li away. To govern its criminal justice from a distance—how could that not breed injustice?"

sentences.zh: 事遂止。

translations.literal: The matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，拜榮祿大夫、湖廣行省平章政事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Branch Secretariat Grand Councillor of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1291 he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Councillor of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 臺臣言其在宗正決獄平，即去，恐難其繼者。

translations.literal: Censorate officials said that in the Imperial Clan Court his judgments in cases were fair, and that if he left at once they feared it would be hard to find a successor.
translations.idiomatic: Censorate officials observed that as Grand Judge his rulings had been exemplary and warned that if he left immediately they might struggle to find a worthy successor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「湖廣之地，朕嘗駐蹕，非斯人不可。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The land of Huguang—I once encamped there; no one but this man will do."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I once encamped in Huguang myself; no one but he can govern it properly."

sentences.zh: 遂行。

translations.literal: He then departed.
translations.idiomatic: He set out for his post.

sentences.zh: 時江湖間盜賊出沒，剽取商旅貨財。

translations.literal: At the time bandits on the rivers and lakes appeared and vanished, plundering the goods and wealth of traveling merchants.
translations.idiomatic: At the time bandits haunted the rivers and lakes, robbing merchants of their goods.

sentences.zh: 哈剌哈孫至，則發卒悉擒誅之，水陸之途始皆無梗。

translations.literal: When Harqasun arrived, he dispatched troops who captured and executed them all; only then were the routes by water and land everywhere unobstructed.
translations.idiomatic: When Harqasun arrived he sent out troops, captured the bandits, and executed them; only then did travel by water and land become safe again.

sentences.zh: 初，樞密置行院於各省，分兵民為二，奸人植黨自蔽。

translations.literal: Earlier the Bureau of Military Affairs had established branch courts in each province, dividing military and civil affairs in two, so that schemers planted factions to shield themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Bureau of Military Affairs had set up branch courts in each province, splitting military and civil authority; corrupt officials used factional networks to shield one another.

sentences.zh: 後因入覲極陳其不便，帝為罷之。

translations.literal: Later, on entering court for audience, he set forth at length its inconveniences, and the emperor abolished it on his account.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he came to court for an audience, he argued forcefully against the arrangement, and the emperor abolished it at his urging.

sentences.zh: 因問曰：「風憲之職，人多言其撓吏治，信乎？」

translations.literal: He then asked: "The office of censorial oversight—many say it obstructs civil administration; is that true?"
translations.idiomatic: He then asked, "Many say the censorate obstructs civil administration—is that true?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「朝廷設此以糾奸慝，貪吏疾之，妄為謗耳。」

translations.literal: He replied: "The court established this to correct treachery and wickedness; corrupt officials hate it and slander it without cause."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The court established the censorate to root out corruption; greedy officials resent it and spread idle slander—that is all."

sentences.zh: 帝然其言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 三十年，平章劉國傑將兵征交趾，哈剌哈孫戒將吏無擾民。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year Grand Councillor Liu Guojie led troops to campaign against Jiaozhi; Harqasun admonished the generals and officials not to disturb the people.
translations.idiomatic: In 1293 Grand Councillor Liu Guojie led an expedition against Jiaozhi; Harqasun strictly ordered the commanders and officials not to harass the populace.

sentences.zh: 會有奪民魚菜者，杖其千戶，軍中肅然。

translations.literal: It happened that someone seized fish and vegetables from the people; he had the chiliarch beaten, and the army became sternly disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: When a soldier seized fish and vegetables from civilians, he had the responsible chiliarch flogged, and discipline in the army became exemplary.

sentences.zh: 俄有旨發湖湘富民萬家，屯田廣西，以圖交趾。

translations.literal: Soon an edict came to mobilize ten thousand wealthy households of Hunan and Xiang for garrison farming in Guangxi, in order to plan against Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict arrived ordering ten thousand wealthy households from Hunan and Xiang to be relocated for garrison farming in Guangxi as a step toward Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 哈剌哈孫密遣使奏曰：「往年遠征無功，瘡痍未復，今又徙民瘴鄉，必將怨叛。」

translations.literal: Harqasun secretly sent a messenger to memorialize: "In former years the distant campaign achieved nothing; wounds are not yet healed; now again to relocate the people to malarial lands will surely breed resentment and rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Harqasun secretly sent a memorial: "The distant campaigns of recent years failed, and the region has not yet recovered. To relocate people now into malarial country will surely provoke resentment and rebellion."

sentences.zh: 吏莫知其奏，抱卷請署，弗荅。

translations.literal: The clerks did not know of his memorial; they brought documents requesting his signature, and he did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks knew nothing of his memorial and brought documents for his signature; he refused.

sentences.zh: 吏再請，則曰：「姑緩之。」

translations.literal: When the clerks asked again, he said: "For the moment, put it off."
translations.idiomatic: When they pressed again he said, "Put it off for now."

sentences.zh: 未幾，使還報罷，民皆感悅。

translations.literal: Before long the messenger returned reporting cancellation; the people were all moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his messenger returned with word that the order had been revoked, and the people were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 及廣西元帥府請募南丹五千戶屯田，事上行省，哈剌哈孫曰：「此土著之民，誠為便之，內足以實空地，外足以制交趾之寇，可不煩士卒而饋餉有餘。」

translations.literal: When the Guangxi Marshal's Office requested to recruit five thousand households of Nandan for garrison farming and reported the matter to the Branch Secretariat, Harqasun said: "These are indigenous people; it is truly convenient for them; inwardly it suffices to fill empty lands, outwardly it suffices to restrain the raiders of Jiaozhi—soldiers need not be troubled and provisions will be more than enough."
translations.idiomatic: When the Guangxi Marshal's Office proposed recruiting five thousand Nandan households for garrison farming and referred the matter to the branch secretariat, Harqasun said, "These are indigenous peoples, and the plan truly suits them: inwardly it will fill empty lands, outwardly it will check Jiaozhi raiders, without burdening the army and with surplus provisions besides."

sentences.zh: 即命度地立為五屯，統以屯長，給牛種農具與之。

translations.literal: He at once ordered land surveyed and five garrison colonies established, placed under garrison chiefs, and gave them oxen, seed, and farm implements.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered land surveyed, established five garrison colonies under garrison chiefs, and supplied oxen, seed, and farm tools.

sentences.zh: 湖南宣慰張國紀建言，欲按唐、宋末徵民間夏稅。

translations.literal: Hunan Pacification Commissioner Zhang Guoji submitted a proposal wishing to levy on the populace the summer tax unpaid at the end of Tang and Song.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan Pacification Commissioner Zhang Guoji proposed levying on the populace the summer tax left uncollected at the fall of Tang and Song.

sentences.zh: 哈剌哈孫曰：「亡國弊政，失寬大之意，聖朝其可行耶？」

translations.literal: Harqasun said: "A perished state's bad policy, losing the spirit of magnanimity—can the sage dynasty carry this out?"
translations.idiomatic: Harqasun said, "That is a ruinous policy of a fallen dynasty, contrary to the spirit of magnanimity—how could the sage dynasty adopt it?"

sentences.zh: 奏止其議。

translations.literal: He memorialized to stop the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to block the proposal.

sentences.zh: 大德二年，入朝上都，成宗拜光祿大夫、江浙行省左丞相。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dade he came to court at Shangdu; Chengzong appointed him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Left Chancellor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1298 he came to court at Shangdu, and Temür appointed him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Left Chancellor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 視政七日，徵拜中書左丞相，進階銀青榮祿大夫。

translations.literal: After seven days in office he was summoned and appointed Left Chancellor of the Central Secretariat, advanced to Silver-Green Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: After only seven days in office he was summoned to the capital as Left Chancellor of the Central Secretariat and promoted to Silver-Green Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 既拜命，斥言利之徒，一以節用愛民為務。

translations.literal: Once he received appointment, he drove away those who spoke of profit, and made frugality and cherishing the people his sole task.
translations.idiomatic: Once appointed he dismissed profit-seeking advisers and devoted himself wholly to frugality and the welfare of the people.

sentences.zh: 有大政事，必引儒臣雜議。

translations.literal: When there were great state affairs, he invariably brought in Confucian officials for joint deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: On major state affairs he invariably consulted Confucian officials alongside other advisers.

sentences.zh: 京師久闕孔子廟，而國學寓他署，乃奏建廟學，選名儒為學官，采近臣子弟入學。

translations.literal: The capital had long lacked a temple to Confucius, while the National University lodged in another office; he memorialized to build temple and school, selected renowned Confucians as school officers, and recruited sons of close ministers to enter study.
translations.idiomatic: The capital had long lacked a Confucian temple, and the National University was housed in borrowed quarters; he memorialized to build a temple-school complex, appointed distinguished Confucian scholars as instructors, and enrolled sons of high officials.

sentences.zh: 又集群議建南郊，為一代定制。

translations.literal: He also gathered a council to discuss establishing the Southern Suburban Altar, making it a fixed regulation for the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: He also convened deliberations on establishing the Southern Suburban Altar, setting a lasting ritual standard for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 五年，同列有以雲南行省左丞劉深計倡議曰：「世祖以神武一海內，功蓋萬世。

translations.literal: In the fifth year a colleague, following the plan of Yunnan Branch Secretariat Left Vice Councillor Liu Shen, initiated a proposal saying: "Shizu with divine martial prowess unified all within the seas; his merit covers ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: In 1301 a colleague, taking up a proposal from Liu Shen, Left Vice Councillor of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat, argued: "Kublai with divine martial prowess unified the realm; his achievements will endure for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 今上嗣大歷服，未有武功以彰休烈，西南夷有八百媳婦國未奉正朔，請往征之。」

translations.literal: The present sovereign has succeeded to the great mandate but has no military achievement to display his glorious virtue; in the southwest there is the country of the Eight Hundred Wives that has not received the correct calendar—please go to campaign against it."
translations.idiomatic: The present sovereign has inherited the great mandate but has no military achievement to display his glorious virtue. In the southwest the Eight Hundred Wives country has not yet accepted our calendar—let us campaign against it."

sentences.zh: 哈剌哈孫曰：「山嶠小夷，遼絕萬里，可諭之使來，不足以煩中國。」

translations.literal: Harqasun said: "A petty Yi of mountain ridges, remote by ten thousand li—it can be instructed to come; it is not worth troubling the Middle Kingdom."
translations.idiomatic: Harqasun said, "They are a petty mountain people ten thousand li away. Send envoys to summon them—that is enough; the empire need not be troubled for such a matter."

sentences.zh: 不聽，竟發兵二萬，命深將以往。

translations.literal: He was not heeded; in the end twenty thousand troops were dispatched, with Shen ordered to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: His counsel was ignored; twenty thousand troops were raised and Liu Shen was ordered to lead them.

sentences.zh: 道出湖廣，民疲於餽餉。

translations.literal: The route passed through Huguang; the people were worn out by supplying provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The route passed through Huguang, and the people were exhausted by supplying the army.

sentences.zh: 及次順元，深脅蛇節求金三千兩、馬三千匹。

translations.literal: When they reached Shunyuan, Shen coerced Shejie to demand three thousand taels of gold and three thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Shunyuan, Liu Shen extorted from Shejie three thousand taels of gold and three thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 蛇節因民不堪，舉兵圍深於窮谷，首尾不能相救。

translations.literal: Shejie, because the people could not bear it, raised troops and besieged Shen in a remote valley; front and rear could not rescue one another.
translations.idiomatic: Shejie, seeing the people could endure no more, rose in arms and trapped Liu Shen in a remote valley; the army's van and rear could not aid each other.

sentences.zh: 事聞，遣平章劉國傑往援，擒蛇節，斬軍中，然士卒存者纔十一二，轉餉者亦如之，訖無成功。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Grand Councillor Liu Guojie was sent to relieve them; Shejie was captured and executed in the army, yet of the soldiers who survived barely one or two in ten, and the transport troops likewise; in the end there was no success.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached court, Grand Councillor Liu Guojie was sent to relieve the force. Shejie was captured and executed in camp, but barely one soldier in ten survived, and the transport troops fared no better; the campaign ended in complete failure.

sentences.zh: 帝始悔不用其言。

translations.literal: The emperor then began to regret not having used his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then regretted not having heeded his advice.

sentences.zh: 會赦，有司議釋深罪。

translations.literal: When an amnesty came, the responsible offices deliberated releasing Shen from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When a general amnesty was proclaimed, officials proposed releasing Liu Shen from punishment.

sentences.zh: 哈剌哈孫曰：「徼名首釁，喪師辱國，非常罪比，不誅無以謝天下。」

translations.literal: Harqasun said: "Seeking fame and being first to provoke trouble, losing the army and shaming the state—this is not comparable to ordinary crimes; if he is not executed there is no way to answer to the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Harqasun said, "He sought glory and provoked war, lost the army and shamed the state—this is no ordinary offense. Unless he is executed there is no answering to the realm."

sentences.zh: 奏誅之。

translations.literal: He memorialized to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for his execution, and it was carried out.

sentences.zh: 七年，進中書右丞相。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was advanced to Right Chancellor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1303 he was promoted to Right Chancellor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 嘗言治道必先守令，近用多不得其人，於是精加遴選，定官吏贓罪十二章及丁憂、婚聘、盜賊等制，禁獻戶及山澤之利。

translations.literal: He once said that in governing the Way one must first have prefects and magistrates; recent appointments often did not obtain the right men; he therefore refined selection, fixed twelve chapters on official corruption and regulations on mourning leave, marriage betrothal, banditry, and the like, and forbade presenting households and profits from mountains and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: He often said that good government begins with capable prefects and magistrates, yet recent appointments had too often missed the mark. He therefore tightened selection, codified twelve articles on official corruption together with rules on mourning, betrothal, and banditry, and banned the presentation of households and monopolies on mountain and marsh resources.

sentences.zh: 每歲車駕幸上都，哈剌哈孫必留守京師。

translations.literal: Every year when the imperial carriage visited Shangdu, Harqasun invariably remained to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Each year when the emperor traveled to Shangdu, Harqasun remained behind to govern the capital.

sentences.zh: 時帝弗豫，制出中宮，群邪黨附，哈剌哈孫以身匡之，天下晏然。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was unwell; policy issued from the inner palace; wicked men formed factions; Harqasun with his person set things right, and the realm was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, policy issued from the inner palace and corrupt factions gathered strength; Harqasun held the state steady by force of character, and the realm remained at peace.

sentences.zh: 十年，加開府儀同三司、監修國史，置僚屬。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was given the additional titles of Commissioner with Equal Protocol to the Three Dukes and Supervisor of the Compilation of the National History, with subordinate officials appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1306 he was additionally appointed Commissioner with Equal Protocol to the Three Dukes and Supervisor of the Compilation of the National History, with a full staff.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，帝寢疾篤甚，入侍醫藥，出總宿衛。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter the emperor's illness grew grave; he entered to attend with medicine, and went out to command the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the emperor's illness grew grave; Harqasun attended him with medicines by day and commanded the palace guard by night.

sentences.zh: 藩王欲入侍疾者不聽；

translations.literal: Princes of the blood who wished to enter to attend the illness were not permitted;
translations.idiomatic: He refused entry to princes who wished to attend the sickbed;

sentences.zh: 日理機務如故。

translations.literal: yet day by day he handled state affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: yet he continued to handle state affairs each day as before.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，成宗崩。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year Chengzong died.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1307 Temür died.

sentences.zh: 時武宗撫軍北邊，仁宗侍太后在懷慶，諸奸臣謀斷北道，請成后垂簾聽政，立安西王阿難荅。

translations.literal: At the time Wuzong was commanding troops on the northern frontier, Renzong attended the empress dowager at Huaiqing; various wicked ministers plotted to cut the northern road, requested that Empress Chengzong hold the curtain and hear government, and install Prince of Anxi Ananda.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong was then commanding troops on the northern frontier while Renzong attended the empress dowager at Huaiqing. Wicked ministers plotted to block the northern road, urged Empress Buluhan to rule from behind the curtain, and sought to install Prince Anxi Ananda as emperor.

sentences.zh: 哈剌哈孫密遣使北迎武宗，南迎仁宗，悉收京城百司符印，封府庫，稱疾卧闕下，內旨日數至，並不聽，文書皆不署。

translations.literal: Harqasun secretly sent envoys north to welcome Wuzong and south to welcome Renzong; he collected all the tallies and seals of the hundred offices in the capital, sealed the treasuries, claimed illness and lay below the palace gates; inner edicts arrived several times daily, and he would not heed them; he signed no documents.
translations.idiomatic: Harqasun secretly sent envoys north to welcome Wuzong and south to welcome Renzong, seized the seals of every capital office, sealed the treasuries, and feigned illness below the palace gates. Inner edicts arrived daily; he ignored them all and signed no document.

sentences.zh: 衆欲害之，未敢發。

translations.literal: The multitude wished to harm him but did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: His enemies wished to kill him but did not dare strike.

sentences.zh: 及仁宗至近郊，衆猶未知也。

translations.literal: When Renzong reached the near suburbs, the multitude still did not know.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong reached the suburbs, the conspirators still knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 三月朔，列牘請署，后決以三月三日御殿聽政，乃立署之，衆大喜，莫知所為。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month documents were arrayed requesting his signature; the empress decided that on the third day of the third month she would ascend the hall and hear government; he then stood and signed them; the multitude was greatly pleased and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the third month documents were laid before him for signature. The empress had decided to take the throne on the third; he signed at once. The conspirators rejoiced, unaware of what was coming.

sentences.zh: 明日，迎仁宗入，執左丞相阿忽台及安西王阿難荅等就誅，內難悉平。

translations.literal: The next day Renzong was welcomed in; Left Chancellor Ahutai and Prince of Anxi Ananda and others were seized and executed on the spot; the inner turmoil was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Renzong entered the capital; Left Chancellor Ahutai, Prince Anxi Ananda, and their confederates were seized and executed, and the palace crisis was ended.

sentences.zh: 自冬至春，未嘗一至家休沐。

translations.literal: From winter to spring he had not once gone home for rest.
translations.idiomatic: From winter through spring he never once went home for rest.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，武宗至自北，即皇帝位，拜太傅、錄軍國重事，仍緫百揆，賜宅一區，以其子脫歡入侍。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer Wuzong arrived from the north and assumed the imperial throne; Harqasun was appointed Grand Preceptor and Recorder of Important Affairs in Military and State, still overseeing all administration; a residence was granted, and his son Tuohuan was admitted to attend the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Wuzong arrived from the north and took the throne. Harqasun was appointed Grand Preceptor and Recorder of Important Affairs in Military and State, retained overall charge of government, granted a residence, and his son Tuohuan was admitted to attend the emperor.

sentences.zh: 初仁宗之入也，阿忽台有勇力，人莫敢近，諸王禿剌實手縛之，以功封越王，三宮盡幸其第，賜與甚厚，以慶元路為其食邑。

translations.literal: When Renzong first entered, Ahutai had martial strength and no one dared approach him; Prince Tula in fact bound him with his own hands; for this merit he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yue; the three palaces all visited his residence; gifts were very generous; Qingyuan Circuit was made his fief.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong first entered the capital, Ahutai was so fierce that none dared approach him until Prince Tula seized him with his own hands. For this service Tula was enfeoffed as Prince of Yue; the three palaces visited his residence and heaped gifts upon him, and Qingyuan Circuit was granted as his fief.

sentences.zh: 哈剌哈孫力爭之，曰：「祖宗之制，非親王不得加一字之封。

translations.literal: Harqasun strove against it, saying: "The institutions of the ancestors—only imperial princes may receive a one-character enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Harqasun argued forcefully: "By ancestral institution, only imperial princes may receive a one-character princely title.

sentences.zh: 禿剌疏屬豈得以一日之功廢萬世之制哉。」

translations.literal: Tula is a distant kinsman—how can one day's merit abolish an institution for ten thousand generations?"
translations.idiomatic: Tula is a distant kinsman—how can a single day's service overturn a rule meant to endure ten thousand generations?"

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not hear him.

sentences.zh: 禿剌因譖於帝曰：「方安西王謀干大統，哈剌哈孫亦嘗署文書。」

translations.literal: Tula therefore slandered him to the emperor, saying: "When the Prince of Anxi was plotting for the great succession, Harqasun also once signed documents."
translations.idiomatic: Tula then slandered him to the emperor: "When Prince Anxi plotted for the throne, Harqasun too once signed documents."

sentences.zh: 由是罷相出鎮北邊。

translations.literal: On this account he was dismissed as chancellor and sent out to guard the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: On this account he was dismissed from the chancellorship and sent to guard the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「和林為北邊重鎮，今諸部降者又百餘萬，非重臣不足以鎮之，念無以易哈剌哈孫者。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "Karakorum is a vital post of the northern frontier; now those tribes that have submitted number more than a million again—no one but a weighty minister suffices to guard it; I consider that there is no one to replace Harqasun."
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "Karakorum is the key to the northern frontier, and more than a million tribesmen have lately submitted. Only a minister of the first rank can hold it—and none can replace Harqasun."

sentences.zh: 賜黃金三百兩、白銀三千五百兩、鈔十五萬貫、帛四萬端、乳馬六十匹，以太傅、左丞相行和林省事。

translations.literal: He was granted three hundred taels of gold, three thousand five hundred taels of silver, one hundred fifty thousand strings of paper money, forty thousand bolts of silk, sixty nursing mares, and as Grand Preceptor and Left Chancellor he administered Karakorum affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted three hundred taels of gold, three thousand five hundred taels of silver, one hundred fifty thousand strings of paper money, forty thousand bolts of silk, and sixty nursing mares, and was sent as Grand Preceptor and Left Chancellor to administer Karakorum.

sentences.zh: 太后亦賜帛二百端、鈔五萬貫。

translations.literal: The empress dowager also granted two hundred bolts of silk and fifty thousand strings of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager also granted two hundred bolts of silk and fifty thousand strings of paper money.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，斬為盜者一人。

translations.literal: On reaching his post, he executed one man for robbery.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post, he executed one man for robbery.

sentences.zh: 分遣使者賑降戶。

translations.literal: He dispatched envoys in separate parties to relieve submitted households.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched envoys in separate parties to relieve submitted households.

sentences.zh: 奏出鈔帛易牛羊以給之，近水者教取魚食。

translations.literal: He memorialized to disburse paper money and silk to exchange for cattle and sheep to supply them; those near water he taught to take fish for food.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to disburse paper money and silk to exchange for cattle and sheep to supply them, and taught those near water to take fish for food.

sentences.zh: 會大雪，民無取得食，命諸部置傳車，相去各三百里，凡十傳，轉米數萬石以餉饑民，不足則益以牛羊。

translations.literal: When heavy snow fell and the people could obtain no food, he ordered the tribes to set up relay carts three hundred li apart, ten relay stages in all, and transfer tens of thousands of piculs of grain to feed the hungry; where that was insufficient, cattle and sheep were added.
translations.idiomatic: When heavy snow fell and the people could obtain no food, he ordered the tribes to set up relay carts three hundred li apart—ten relay stages in all—and transfer tens of thousands of piculs of grain to feed the hungry, supplementing with cattle and sheep where needed.

sentences.zh: 又度地置內倉，積粟以待來者。

translations.literal: He also measured land and established inner granaries, storing grain to await those who came.
translations.idiomatic: He also measured land and established inner granaries, storing grain for those who came.

sentences.zh: 浚古渠，溉田數千頃。

translations.literal: He dredged ancient canals and irrigated several thousand qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged ancient canals and irrigated several thousand qing of fields.

sentences.zh: 治稱海屯田，教部落雜耕其間，歲得米二十餘萬。

translations.literal: He organized Changhai garrison farms, teaching the tribes to farm mixed crops among them, yielding more than two hundred thousand piculs of grain per year.
translations.idiomatic: He organized Changhai garrison farms, teaching the tribes to farm mixed crops there, yielding more than two hundred thousand piculs of grain per year.

sentences.zh: 北邊大治。

translations.literal: The northern frontier was greatly pacified and prospered.
translations.idiomatic: The northern frontier was greatly pacified and prospered.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，賜大帳，如諸王諸藩禮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was granted a great tent, with ceremony like that for princes and feudatories.
translations.idiomatic: In 1308 he was granted a great tent with ceremony like that for princes and feudatories.

sentences.zh: 〔閏〕十一月，寢疾，語其屬曰：「吾不復能佐理國事矣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month [intercalary], he fell gravely ill and told his subordinates, "I can no longer assist in managing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eleventh month he fell gravely ill and told his subordinates, "I can no longer assist in managing state affairs.

sentences.zh: 行省之務，汝曹勉之，毋貽朝廷憂。」

translations.literal: As for the branch secretariat's duties, you must exert yourselves and not bring worry to the court."
translations.idiomatic: As for the branch secretariat's duties, you must exert yourselves and not bring worry to the court."

sentences.zh: 薨，年五十二。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，驚悼曰：「喪我賢相。」

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he was startled and grieved, saying, "I have lost my worthy chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he was startled and grieved, saying, "I have lost my worthy chancellor."

sentences.zh: 賻鈔二萬五千貫。

translations.literal: Funeral gifts of twenty-five thousand strings of paper money were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral gifts of twenty-five thousand strings of paper money were granted.

sentences.zh: 詔歸葬昌平，追贈推誠履政佐運功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國，追封順德王，諡忠獻。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his return for burial at Changping; he was posthumously granted the title of Meritorious Minister for Sincerity in Trust, Conduct in Government, and Assistance in Destiny, Grand Preceptor, Commissioner with Equal Protocol to the Three Dukes, and Upper Pillar of the State; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Shunde with the posthumous name Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his return for burial at Changping. He was posthumously granted the title Meritorious Minister for Sincerity in Trust, Conduct in Government, and Assistance in Destiny, made Grand Preceptor, Commissioner with Equal Protocol to the Three Dukes, and Upper Pillar of the State, and enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Shunde with the posthumous name Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 子脫歡，由太子賓客拜御史中丞，襲號荅剌罕，進御史大夫，行臺江南。

translations.literal: His son Tuohuan, from Preceptor of the Crown Prince was appointed Censor-in-Chief, inherited the title Darqan, was advanced to Censor-in-Chief, and administered the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tuohuan rose from Preceptor of the Crown Prince to Censor-in-Chief, inherited the title Darqan, was promoted to Chief Censor, and served on the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.

sentences.zh: 尋拜平章，行省江浙，進左丞相，兼領行宣政院。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Councillor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, advanced to Left Chancellor, and concurrently headed the Branch Commission for Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Grand Councillor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, promoted to Left Chancellor, and concurrently headed the Branch Commission for Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs.

sentences.zh: 重厚有父風，喜讀書，為政不尚苛暴，得衆心。

translations.literal: Grave and weighty, he had his father's manner; he delighted in reading; in government he did not esteem harsh severity and won the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Grave and weighty like his father, he loved learning, governed without harshness, and won the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 致和元年，卒于官，年三十七。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhihe he died in office, aged thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In 1328 he died in office at the age of thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 子蠻蠻。

translations.literal: His son was Manman.
translations.idiomatic: He left a son, Manman.

sentences.zh: 阿沙不花

translations.literal: Ashabuhua
translations.idiomatic: Ashabuhua

sentences.zh: 阿沙不花者，康里國王族也。

translations.literal: Ashabuhua was of the royal clan of Kangli.
translations.idiomatic: Ashabuhua belonged to the royal clan of Kangli.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖拔康里時，其祖母苫滅古麻里氏新寡，有二子，曰曲律、牙牙，皆幼，而國亂家破無所依，欲去而歸朝廷，念無以自達。

translations.literal: In the beginning, when Taizu conquered Kangli, his grandmother Shamiegu Malishi was newly widowed; she had two sons, named Qulu and Yaya, both young; the state was in turmoil and the family broken with nowhere to rely; she wished to go and return to the court but thought there was no way to reach it herself.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu conquered Kangli, his grandmother Shamiegu Malishi was newly widowed, with two young sons named Qulu and Yaya. The realm was in chaos and the family ruined, with nowhere to turn; she wished to flee east to submit to the court but saw no way to reach it.

sentences.zh: 一夕有數駝皆重負突入營中，驅之不去。

translations.literal: One night several camels, all heavily laden, burst into the camp; driven, they would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: One night several heavily laden camels burst into the camp and could not be driven away.

sentences.zh: 旦乃繫駝營外，置所負其旁，夜復納營中，候有求者歸之。

translations.literal: At dawn she tethered the camels outside the camp, placed their burdens beside them, at night brought them back into camp, and waited for anyone who came seeking to return them.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn she tethered them outside the camp with their loads beside them, brought them back in at night, and waited for an owner to claim them.

sentences.zh: 如是十餘日，終無求者。

translations.literal: Thus for more than ten days, in the end no one came seeking them.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten days no one came to claim them.

sentences.zh: 乃發視其裝，皆西域重寶。

translations.literal: She then opened and looked at their packs—all were heavy treasures of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: She opened the packs and found them filled with precious goods from the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 驚曰：「殆天欲資我而東耶，不然，此豈吾所宜有。」

translations.literal: Startled, she said: "Perhaps Heaven wishes to supply me for going east? Otherwise, how could these be what I ought to possess?"
translations.idiomatic: Startled, she exclaimed, "Has Heaven sent these to supply our journey east? Otherwise, how could such wealth be meant for us?"

sentences.zh: 遂驅馳載二子越數國至京師。

translations.literal: She then drove swiftly, carrying her two sons across several states to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: She then drove swiftly east with her two sons across many lands until they reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 時太祖已崩，太宗立，盡獻其所有，帝深異之，命有司治邸舍、具廩餼以居焉。

translations.literal: At the time Taizu had died and Taizong was enthroned; she presented all she possessed; the emperor was deeply struck and ordered the responsible offices to prepare a residence and supply provisions for her dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had died and Ögedei was now emperor. She presented everything she had brought, and the emperor, deeply impressed, ordered officials to prepare a residence and provisions for her.

sentences.zh: 居二年，聞國中已定，謁帝欲歸。

translations.literal: After dwelling two years, hearing that the state was settled, she came to audience with the emperor wishing to return.
translations.idiomatic: After two years she heard that Kangli was at peace and came to court to ask leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「汝昔何為而來，今何為而去？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In former days for what did you come, and now for what do you go?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Why did you come then, and why do you wish to leave now?"

sentences.zh: 且問其所欲。

translations.literal: He also asked what she desired.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked what she wanted.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣妾昔以國亂無主，遠歸陛下，今賴陛下威德，聞國已定，欲歸守墳墓耳。

translations.literal: She replied: "Your subject formerly, because the state was in turmoil without a ruler, came from afar to submit to Your Majesty; now relying on Your Majesty's august virtue, hearing the state is settled, I wish only to return and guard the graves.
translations.idiomatic: She replied, "Your subject came from afar when our land was torn by chaos and had no lord. Now, thanks to Your Majesty's power and virtue, I hear the realm is settled and wish only to return and tend the ancestral graves.

sentences.zh: 妾惟二子，雖愚無知，願留事陛下。」

translations.literal: I have only these two sons; though foolish and without knowledge, I wish them to remain to serve Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: I have only these two sons. Though they are simple youths, I beg leave for them to remain in Your Majesty's service."

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，立召二子入宿衛，而禮遣之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, at once summoned the two sons into the palace guard, and sent her off with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, immediately enrolled both sons in the palace guard, and sent her home with full honors.

sentences.zh: 後十三年復來，則二子已從憲宗伐蜀矣。

translations.literal: Thirteen years later she came again; the two sons had already followed Möngke in campaigning against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen years later she returned, only to find that both sons had already joined Möngke's campaign against Shu.

sentences.zh: 逮至和寧，聞憲宗崩，諸將皆還，而二子獨後，心方以為憂。

translations.literal: When she reached Hening, she heard Möngke had died; the generals all returned, but the two sons alone lagged behind; her heart was just then filled with worry.
translations.idiomatic: When she reached Hening she learned that Möngke had died and that the generals were returning, yet her sons had not come back. She grew deeply anxious.

sentences.zh: 過一古廟，因入禱焉，若聞神語，連稱「好好」而不知其故，問其國人通漢語者，知為吉語。

translations.literal: Passing an ancient temple, she entered to pray; as if hearing a divine voice, it repeatedly called "hao hao" and she did not know the reason; asking a countryman who understood Chinese, she learned it was an auspicious phrase.
translations.idiomatic: Passing an ancient temple, she went in to pray. She seemed to hear a spirit voice repeating the Chinese words "good, good"—and did not understand until a compatriot who knew Chinese told her it was an auspicious omen.

sentences.zh: 還至舍，則二子已至矣。

translations.literal: Returning to her lodging, the two sons had already arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When she returned to her lodging, both sons were already there.

sentences.zh: 遂留居焉。

translations.literal: She then remained to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: She settled there and remained.

sentences.zh: 曲律無子。

translations.literal: Qulu had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: Qulu left no sons.

sentences.zh: 牙牙後封康國王，生六子，阿沙不花最賢，年十四，入侍世祖。

translations.literal: Yaya was later enfeoffed as King of Kang and had six sons; Ashabuhua was the most worthy; at fourteen he entered to attend Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Yaya was later enfeoffed as King of Kang and had six sons. Ashabuhua, the most gifted, entered imperial service at fourteen under Kublai.

sentences.zh: 世祖賜土田、給奴隸，使居興和之天城。

translations.literal: Shizu granted land and fields, provided slaves, and had him dwell at Tiancheng in Xinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai granted him lands and slaves and had him reside at Tiancheng in Xinghe.

sentences.zh: 會西蕃遣使者有所奏請，既諭遣之，後數日，帝問近侍諸大臣曰：「前日西使何請，朕何辭以遣？」

translations.literal: It happened that Tibet sent envoys with a memorial request; after they were instructed and dismissed, several days later the emperor asked the close attendants and various ministers: "What did the western envoy request the other day, and with what words did I dismiss him?"
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetan envoys came with a petition, Kublai received and dismissed them. Days later he asked his close ministers, "What did the Tibetan envoy request the other day, and what answer did I give?"

sentences.zh: 諸大臣莫能對，阿沙不花從旁代對甚詳悉。

translations.literal: The various ministers could not answer; Ashabuhua from the side replied in their stead, very fully and in detail.
translations.idiomatic: None of the ministers could answer. Ashabuhua, standing to one side, replied in full detail.

sentences.zh: 帝因怒諸大臣曰：「卿等任天下之重，如此反不若一童子耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor therefore angrily said to the various ministers: "You bear the weight of the realm—yet in this you are not even equal to one boy?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor angrily told the ministers, "You bear the weight of the empire—yet you are outdone by a boy?"

sentences.zh: 嘗扈從上都，方入朝，而宮草多露，跣足而行，帝御大安閣，望而見之，指以為侍臣戒。

translations.literal: Once when attending the emperor at Shangdu, just as he was entering court the palace grass was heavy with dew; he walked barefoot; the emperor was at the Da'an Pavilion, saw him from afar, and pointed to him as a warning to attending ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while attending the emperor at Shangdu, he was entering court barefoot through dew-heavy grass. Kublai, looking down from the Da'an Pavilion, pointed him out as an example to the attending ministers.

sentences.zh: 一日，故命諸門衛勿納阿沙不花。

translations.literal: One day he deliberately ordered the gate guards not to admit Ashabuhua.
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor deliberately ordered the gate guards not to admit Ashabuhua.

sentences.zh: 阿沙不花至，諸門衛皆不納，乃從水竇中入。

translations.literal: When Ashabuhua arrived, none of the gate guards would admit him; he then entered through the water conduit.
translations.idiomatic: When Ashabuhua arrived, every gate guard turned him away, so he entered through a water conduit.

sentences.zh: 帝問故，以實對，且曰：「臣一日不入侍，身將何歸？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason; he answered truthfully and said: "If your subject does not attend for one day, where shall his person go?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why. He answered frankly: "If I miss even one day in attendance, where else can I belong?"

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，更諭諸門衛聽其出入。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and again instructed the gate guards to allow his coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and ordered the gate guards to let him pass freely.

sentences.zh: 命飭四宿衛兵器，無敢或慢；

translations.literal: He was ordered to inspect the weapons of the four palace guards; none dared be negligent;
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to inspect the arms of the four palace guard units, and none dared neglect their duty;

sentences.zh: 復使掌門，無取闌入。

translations.literal: he was again made to control the gates, with no one allowed to force entry.
translations.idiomatic: he was again put in charge of the gates and barred unauthorized entry.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「可用矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "He can be employed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "He is ready for greater service."

sentences.zh: 乃顏叛，諸王納牙等皆應之。

translations.literal: Nayan rebelled; Princes Nayi and others all responded to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Nayan rebelled, Prince Nayi and other princes rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 帝問計將安出，對曰：「臣愚以為莫若先撫安諸王，乃行天討，則叛者勢自孤矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked what plan should be adopted; he replied: "Your subject foolishly thinks that nothing is better than first pacifying and reassuring the princes, then carrying out Heaven's punishment—then the rebel's strength will of itself be isolated."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked what should be done. He replied, "Your subject believes we should first reassure the princes, then carry out Heaven's punishment. The rebel's strength will then collapse of itself."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善，卿試為朕行之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good—try to carry this out for me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said—go and do this for me."

sentences.zh: 即北說納牙曰：「大王聞乃顏反耶？」

translations.literal: He at once went north and said to Nayi: "Great Prince, have you heard that Nayan has rebelled?"
translations.idiomatic: He went north at once and said to Nayi, "Great Prince, have you heard that Nayan has rebelled?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「聞之。」

translations.literal: He said: "I have heard."
translations.idiomatic: Nayi said, "I have."

sentences.zh: 曰：「大王知乃顏已遣使自歸耶？」

translations.literal: He said: "Great Prince, do you know Nayan has already sent envoys to submit of himself?"
translations.idiomatic: Ashabuhua said, "Do you know that Nayan has already sent envoys to submit?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「不知也。」

translations.literal: He said: "I did not know."
translations.idiomatic: Nayi said, "I did not."

sentences.zh: 曰：「聞大王等皆欲為乃顏外應，今乃顏既自歸矣，是獨大王與主上抗。

translations.literal: He said: "I have heard that you great princes all wished to respond to Nayan from outside; now Nayan has already submitted of himself—this means the Great Prince alone stands against the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Ashabuhua said, "I hear that you princes meant to support Nayan from outside. Now that he has submitted, you alone would stand against the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 幸主上聖明，亦知非大王意，置之不問。

translations.literal: Fortunately the sovereign is sage and bright and also knows this was not the Great Prince's intent, and has set it aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately the sovereign is wise and knows this was not your intent, and has set the matter aside.

sentences.zh: 然二三大臣不能無惑，大王何不往見上自陳，為萬全計。」

translations.literal: Yet two or three great ministers cannot be without doubts—why does the Great Prince not go to see the sovereign and explain himself, as a plan for complete security?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet a few ministers still harbor doubts. Why not go to court and explain yourself—that would be the surest course."

sentences.zh: 納牙悅許之。

translations.literal: Nayi gladly agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Nayi gladly agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是諸王之謀皆解。

translations.literal: On this account the princes' plots were all dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: The princes' conspiracy thus collapsed.

sentences.zh: 阿沙不花還報，帝乃議親征，命徵兵遼陽，以千戶帥昔寶赤之衆從行。

translations.literal: Ashabuhua returned to report; the emperor then deliberated a personal campaign, ordered troops levied in Liaoyang, and had the chiliarch commander Xibaochi's forces follow on the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Ashabuhua returned to report. The emperor then decided on a personal campaign, ordered troops levied in Liaoyang, and took the force of the chiliarch commander Xibaochi with him.

sentences.zh: 及乃顏平，阿沙不花以大同、興和兩郡當車駕所經有帷臺嶺者，數十里無居民，請詔有司作室嶺中，徙邑民百戶居之，割境內昔寶赤牧地使耕種以自養，從之。

translations.literal: When Nayan was pacified, Ashabuhua, because in Datong and Xinghe circuits along the route of the imperial carriage lay Weitai Ridge, where for several tens of li there were no inhabitants, requested an edict that the responsible offices build dwellings in the ridge, relocate a hundred households of townsmen to dwell there, and carve out within the territory Xibaochi's pasture lands for cultivation to support themselves—the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: After Nayan was defeated, Ashabuhua noted that along the imperial route through Datong and Xinghe lay Weitai Ridge, where for miles there were no inhabitants. He memorialized for dwellings to be built on the ridge, a hundred local households relocated there, and part of Xibaochi's pasture within the territory set aside for farming to support them. The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 阿沙不花既領昔寶赤，帝復欲盡徙興和桃山數十村之民，以其地為昔寶赤牧地。

translations.literal: After Ashabuhua had taken charge of Xibaochi, the emperor again wished to relocate entirely the people of several tens of villages of Taoshan in Xinghe, making their lands Xibaochi's pasture.
translations.idiomatic: After Ashabuhua took command of Xibaochi's force, the emperor again proposed relocating all the people of several dozen Taoshan villages in Xinghe to make the land pasture for Xibaochi.

sentences.zh: 阿沙不花固請存三千戶以給鷹食，帝皆聽納。

translations.literal: Ashabuhua firmly requested that three thousand households be retained to supply food for the hunting hawks; the emperor heard and accepted all.
translations.idiomatic: Ashabuhua firmly petitioned to keep three thousand households to supply food for the hunting hawks, and the emperor granted both requests.

sentences.zh: 民德之，至今飲食必祭。

translations.literal: The people were grateful to him; to this day at meals they invariably offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The people were grateful to him; to this day they still offer food in his memory at every meal.

sentences.zh: 至元三十年，海都叛，成宗以皇孫撫軍於北。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Zhiyuan, Haidu rebelled; Chengzong, as imperial grandson, commanded troops on the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In 1293 Haidu rebelled, and Temür, as imperial grandson, commanded troops on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 阿沙不花從行，踰金山戰杭海有功。

translations.literal: Ashabuhua accompanied the expedition, crossed Jinshan, fought at Hang Hai, and performed meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: Ashabuhua accompanied the campaign, crossed Jinshan, fought at Hang Hai, and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 成宗即位，會大宗正扎魯火赤脫兒速以贓污聞，詔鞫問之，脫兒速伏罪，就命代之。

translations.literal: When Chengzong took the throne, it happened that the Grand Chancellor of the Great Court Zarluhuochi Tuoersu was reported for corruption; an edict ordered him interrogated; Tuoersu confessed guilt and Ashabuhua was appointed in his place.
translations.idiomatic: When Temür took the throne, Grand Chancellor of the Great Court Zarluhuochi Tuoersu was reported for corruption. An edict ordered his interrogation; after Tuoersu confessed, Ashabuhua was appointed in his place.

sentences.zh: 成宗目之曰阿即剌。

translations.literal: Chengzong looked at him and called him Aijila.
translations.idiomatic: Temür looked at him and called him Aijila.

sentences.zh: 阿即剌，譯言閻羅王也。

translations.literal: Aijila means Yama, King of the Underworld.
translations.idiomatic: Aijila means Yama, King of the Underworld.

sentences.zh: 有訴朱清、張瑄陰私，既抵罪，帝遣兵馬都指揮使忽剌朮籍沒其家，以受賂誅。

translations.literal: When Zhu Qing and Zhang Xuan were accused of secret misconduct and convicted, the emperor sent the Commander of Military and Horse Hulazhu to register and confiscate their households; he was executed for accepting bribes.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Qing and Zhang Xuan were accused of secret misconduct and convicted, the emperor sent Military and Horse Commander Hulazhu to confiscate their property; Hulazhu was executed for taking bribes.

sentences.zh: 更命阿沙不花往，具以實聞，賜宅一區、鈔萬五千緡，兼兩城兵馬都指揮使事。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Ashabuhua to go instead; he reported the full truth and was granted one residence and fifteen thousand strings of paper money, and concurrently administered military and horse affairs for both circuits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent Ashabuhua instead. He reported the full truth, was granted a residence and fifteen thousand strings of paper money, and concurrently administered military and horse affairs for both circuits.

sentences.zh: 武宗時為懷寧王，總軍漠北，問：「今日材可大用者為誰？」

translations.literal: When Wuzong was Prince of Huaining, commanding troops in the northern deserts, he asked, "Who today has talent fit for great employment?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong was Prince of Huaining, commanding troops in the northern deserts, he asked, "Who today has talent fit for great employment?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「母弟脫脫將相才也，無以易之。」

translations.literal: He replied, "My younger uterine brother Toto has talent for generalship and chancellorship; none can replace him."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "My younger uterine brother Toto has talent for generalship and chancellorship; none can replace him."

sentences.zh: 遂命從行，後果為名臣。

translations.literal: Wuzong then ordered Toto to accompany him, and he later indeed became a renowned minister.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong then ordered Toto to accompany him, and he later became a renowned minister.

sentences.zh: 成宗崩，安西王阿難荅乘間謀繼大統，成后及丞相阿忽台、諸王迷里帖木兒皆陰為之助。

translations.literal: When Chengzong died, Prince of Anxi Ananda seized the interval to plot succession to the great mandate; Empress Chengzong and Chancellor Ahutai and Prince Miritemur all secretly aided him.
translations.idiomatic: When Temür died, Prince Anxi Ananda seized the moment to plot for the throne; Empress Buluhan, Chancellor Ahutai, and Prince Miritemur all secretly supported him.

sentences.zh: 時武宗猶在北邊，太后及仁宗亦在懷孟未至。

translations.literal: At the time Wuzong was still on the northern frontier, and the empress dowager and Renzong were also in Huaimeng and had not arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong was still on the northern frontier, and the empress dowager and Renzong had not yet reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 適武宗遣脫脫計事京師，丞相哈剌哈孫令急還報武宗，而成后已密諭通政使只兒哈郎止其驛馬。

translations.literal: It happened that Wuzong had sent Toto to plan affairs in the capital; Chancellor Harqasun ordered him to return swiftly to report to Wuzong, but Empress Chengzong had secretly instructed Transmission Commissioner Zhirhalang to stop his relay horses.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong had sent Toto to assess affairs in the capital. Chancellor Harqasun ordered him to return at once to report to Wuzong, but Empress Buluhan had secretly instructed Transmission Commissioner Zhirhalang to halt his relay horses.

sentences.zh: 阿沙不花知事急，與同知通政院事察乃謀，作先日署文書給馬去。

translations.literal: Ashabuhua, knowing the matter was urgent, plotted with Associate Administrator of the Transmission Office Chana, forged documents signed on a previous day, and gave horses to depart.
translations.idiomatic: Ashabuhua, seeing how urgent matters were, conspired with Associate Administrator of the Transmission Office Chana to forge documents dated to an earlier day and sent Toto off with relay horses.

sentences.zh: 只兒哈郎聞脫脫已去，方詰問吏，閱案牘乃止。

translations.literal: When Zhirhalang heard Toto had already gone, he then interrogated the clerks; on examining the case documents he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhirhalang learned Toto had already departed, he questioned the clerks, but on examining the records he could do nothing.

sentences.zh: 太后及仁宗既至京師，有言安西王謀以三月三日偽賀仁宗千秋節，因以舉事者。

translations.literal: After the empress dowager and Renzong had reached the capital, there were those who said the Prince of Anxi plotted on the third day of the third month to feign congratulating Renzong on his birthday and thereby launch his action.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress dowager and Renzong reached the capital, word spread that Prince Anxi planned on the third day of the third month to feign congratulations on Renzong's birthday and rise in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 阿沙不花言之哈剌哈孫，且曰：「先人者勝，後人者敗。

translations.literal: Ashabuhua told Harqasun, and said: "He who acts first wins; he who acts later is defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Ashabuhua told Harqasun, "He who strikes first wins; he who waits is lost.

sentences.zh: 后一垂簾聽政，我等皆受制於人矣，不若先事而起。」

translations.literal: Once the empress holds the curtain and hears government, we will all be controlled by others—better to act first and rise."
translations.idiomatic: Once the empress rules from behind the curtain we shall all be at others' mercy. Better to strike first."

sentences.zh: 哈剌哈孫曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Harqasun said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Harqasun said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 乃前二日白仁宗，詐稱武宗遣使召安西王計事，至即執送上都。

translations.literal: Two days beforehand he informed Renzong, falsely saying Wuzong had sent envoys summoning the Prince of Anxi to discuss affairs; when he arrived he was seized and sent up to Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Two days earlier he informed Renzong, sent word under pretense that Wuzong had summoned Prince Anxi for consultation, and seized him on arrival and sent him to Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 盡誅丞相阿忽台以下諸姦臣。

translations.literal: All the wicked ministers from Chancellor Ahutai downward were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Ahutai and the other conspirators were all executed.

sentences.zh: 與哈剌哈孫皆居禁中。

translations.literal: He and Harqasun both dwelt within the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: He and Harqasun both remained within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 仁宗以太子監國，遣使北迎武宗，而武宗遲迴不進，遣使還報太后曰：「非阿沙不花往不可。」

translations.literal: Renzong as crown prince supervised the state, sent envoys north to welcome Wuzong, but Wuzong hesitated and did not advance; he sent envoys back to report to the empress dowager: "Unless Ashabuhua goes, it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Renzong, supervising the state as crown prince, sent envoys north to welcome Wuzong, but Wuzong hesitated. He sent word back to the empress dowager: "Only Ashabuhua can bring him."

sentences.zh: 乃遣奉衣帽、尚醞以往，至野馬川，見武宗，備道兩宮意，及陳安西王謀變始末，且言：「太子監國所以備他變，以待陛下，臣萬死保其無他。」

translations.literal: He was then sent bearing robes, caps, and imperial wine; reaching Yemachuan, he saw Wuzong, fully reported the intentions of the two palaces, and set forth the beginning and end of Prince Anxi's plot, saying moreover: "The crown prince supervises the state in order to guard against other changes and await Your Majesty—I would die ten thousand deaths to guarantee he has no other intent."
translations.idiomatic: He was sent with robes, caps, and imperial wine. At Yemachuan he met Wuzong, conveyed the wishes of both palaces, recounted Prince Anxi's conspiracy from start to finish, and said, "The crown prince governs the realm only to guard against other changes and await Your Majesty. I stake my life on his loyalty."

sentences.zh: 武宗大悅，解衣衣之，拜中書平章政事，軍國大事並聽裁決。

translations.literal: Wuzong was greatly pleased, removed his own garment to clothe him, appointed him Central Secretariat Grand Councillor, and entrusted all great affairs of army and state to his judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong was delighted, gave him his own robe, appointed him Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat, and entrusted all military and civil affairs to his judgment.

sentences.zh: 因奏平內難之有功者燕只哥以下十人為兵馬指揮、為直省舍人。

translations.literal: He thereupon memorialized that the ten men meritorious in pacifying the inner turmoil, from Yanzige downward, be made horse-and-troop commanders and direct secretariat attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to reward ten men who had helped quell the crisis, from Yanzige downward, as horse-and-troop commanders and direct secretariat attendants.

sentences.zh: 詔先奉蒲萄酒及錦綺還報兩宮。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him first to present grape wine and brocade silks in return to report to the two palaces.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered first to send grape wine and brocade silks back to the two palaces as his report.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即日率群臣出迎。

translations.literal: Renzong that same day led the various ministers out to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Renzong led the ministers out to welcome Wuzong.

sentences.zh: 武宗入上都，加阿沙不花特進、太尉，依前平章政事。

translations.literal: When Wuzong entered Shangdu, Ashabuhua was given the additional titles of Special Advancement and Grand Commandant, retaining his former post as Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong entered Shangdu, Ashabuhua was promoted to Special Advancement and Grand Commandant while retaining his post as Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 命與丞相塔思不花還京師治安西王黨，諸連坐囊加真等三十餘人，皆釋之。

translations.literal: He was ordered with Chancellor Tasibuhua to return to the capital to settle the Prince of Anxi faction; all more than thirty persons implicated, including Nangajin, were released.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered with Chancellor Tasibuhua to return to the capital and settle the Prince Anxi faction. More than thirty persons implicated, including Nangajin, were all released.

sentences.zh: 嘗命出太府金分賜諸王貴戚及近侍，方出朝，見一人倉皇若有所懼狀，曰：「此必盜金者。」

translations.literal: Once he was ordered to take gold from the Imperial Treasury to distribute among princes, noble kin, and close attendants; just as he was leaving court he saw a man in frantic haste as if afraid, and said: "This must be the gold thief."
translations.idiomatic: Once, ordered to distribute Imperial Treasury gold among princes, nobles, and close attendants, he was leaving court when he saw a man fleeing in panic and said, "That must be the thief."

sentences.zh: 召詰問之，果得黃金五十兩、白金百兩以聞，就以金賜之，命誅盜者。

translations.literal: He summoned and interrogated him; indeed fifty taels of gold and one hundred taels of white metal were recovered and reported; he then granted him the gold and ordered the thief executed.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned and questioned the man and recovered fifty taels of gold and one hundred taels of silver. He reported the find, gave the gold to the informer, and ordered the thief executed.

sentences.zh: 辭曰：「盜誅固當，金非臣所宜得，願還金以贖盜死。」

translations.literal: He declined, saying: "The thief's execution is certainly fitting, but the gold is not what your subject ought to receive—I wish to return the gold to ransom the thief from death."
translations.idiomatic: He declined: "The thief deserves death, but the gold is not mine to keep. I beg to return it to spare the thief's life."

sentences.zh: 帝悅而從之。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and followed his wish.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and agreed.

sentences.zh: 有近臣蹴踘帝前，帝即命出鈔十五萬貫賜之。

translations.literal: A close attendant played cuju before the emperor; the emperor at once ordered one hundred fifty thousand strings of paper money given him.
translations.idiomatic: A close attendant played cuju before the emperor, who at once ordered one hundred fifty thousand strings of paper money given him as a reward.

sentences.zh: 阿沙不花頓首言曰：「以蹴踘而受上賞，則奇技淫巧之人日進，而賢者日退矣，將如國家何。

translations.literal: Ashabuhua bowed his head and said: "If for cuju one receives a supreme reward, then men of strange skills and licentious craft will advance day by day, and worthy men will retreat day by day—what will become of the state?
translations.idiomatic: Ashabuhua kowtowed and said, "If cuju wins a supreme reward, men of frivolous skill will advance daily and worthy men retreat daily—what will become of the state?

sentences.zh: 臣死不敢奉詔。」

translations.literal: Your subject would die rather than obey such an edict."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject would rather die than carry out such an order."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The reward was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The reward was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 帝又嘗御五花殿，丞相塔思不花、三寶奴，中丞伯顏等侍。

translations.literal: The emperor also once presided at the Wuhua Hall; Chancellor Tasibuhua, Sanbaonu, Vice Censor-in-Chief Bayan, and others attended.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once held court in the Wuhua Hall with Chancellor Tasibuhua, Sanbaonu, Vice Censor-in-Chief Bayan, and others in attendance.

sentences.zh: 阿沙不花見帝容色日悴，乃進曰：「八珍之味不知御，萬金之身不知愛，此古人所戒也。

translations.literal: Ashabuhua, seeing the emperor's complexion daily more haggard, advanced and said: "The flavors of the eight delicacies you do not know how to partake of; a body worth ten thousand in gold you do not know how to cherish—this is what the ancients warned against.
translations.idiomatic: Ashabuhua, seeing the emperor's face grow daily more haggard, admonished him: "You neglect the finest foods and fail to cherish a body worth ten thousand in gold—the ancients warned against this.

sentences.zh: 陛下不思祖宗付託之重，天下仰望之切，而惟糱是沉，姬嬪是好，是猶兩斧伐孤樹，未有不顛仆者也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not think of the weight of the ancestors' entrustment or the realm's eager expectation, but sinks only in fermented grain and favors only imperial consorts—this is like two axes hewing a lone tree; there has never been one that did not topple.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty gives no thought to the weight the ancestors placed upon you or to the realm's eager hopes, but sinks only into wine and dotes only on palace women. That is like two axes hewing a lone tree—it cannot fail to fall.

sentences.zh: 且陛下之天下，祖宗之天下也，陛下之位，祖宗之位也，陛下縱不自愛，如宗社何？」

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty's realm is the ancestors' realm; Your Majesty's throne is the ancestors' throne; even if Your Majesty will not cherish yourself, what of the altars of soil and grain?"
translations.idiomatic: Your realm is the ancestors' realm and your throne the ancestors' throne. Even if you will not cherish yourself, what of the altars of state?"

sentences.zh: 帝大悅曰：「非卿孰為朕言。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and said: "If not you, who would speak thus to me?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and said, "If not you, who would speak such words to me?

sentences.zh: 繼自今毋愛於言，朕不忘也。」

translations.literal: From now on do not spare your words—I shall not forget."
translations.idiomatic: From now on speak freely—I shall not forget."

sentences.zh: 因命進酒。

translations.literal: He then ordered wine brought forward.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered wine served.

sentences.zh: 阿沙不花頓首謝曰：「臣方欲陛下節飲而反勸之，是臣之言不信於陛下也，臣不敢奉詔。」

translations.literal: Ashabuhua bowed his head in thanks and said: "Your subject was just now urging Your Majesty to moderate drinking, yet now I would encourage it—this means your subject's words are not trusted by Your Majesty; your subject dares not obey the edict."
translations.idiomatic: Ashabuhua kowtowed and said, "I have just urged Your Majesty to drink in moderation. To encourage you now would make my words untrustworthy. I dare not obey."

sentences.zh: 左右皆賀帝得直臣。

translations.literal: Those at left and right all congratulated the emperor on gaining a straight-speaking minister.
translations.idiomatic: Those present all congratulated the emperor on gaining a loyal remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 遂進開府儀同三司、中書右丞相，行御史大夫。

translations.literal: He was then advanced to Commissioner with Equal Protocol to the Three Dukes, Right Chancellor of the Central Secretariat, and acting Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to Commissioner with Equal Protocol to the Three Dukes, Right Chancellor of the Central Secretariat, and acting Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 俄復平章政事、錄軍國重事，兼廣武〔康里〕侍衞親軍都指揮使，封康國公。

translations.literal: Soon he was again appointed Grand Councillor and Recorder of Important Affairs in Military and State, concurrently Commander of the Guangwu Kangli Palace Guard and Personal Army, and enfeoffed as Duke of Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed Grand Councillor and Recorder of Important Affairs in Military and State, concurrently made commander of the Guangwu Kangli palace guard and personal army, and enfeoffed as Duke of Kang.

sentences.zh: 有以左道惑眾者，諸世臣大家多信趨之，竟置于法。

translations.literal: When someone used heterodox ways to delude the masses, many great hereditary houses and clans believed and flocked to him; in the end he was punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: When a man used heterodox teachings to mislead the people, many great hereditary houses believed and followed him; in the end he was punished by law.

sentences.zh: 遷知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administer the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to administer the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 以至大二年十月薨于位，年四十七。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Zhide he died in office at the age of forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of 1309 he died in office at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 至正元年，贈純誠一德正憲保大功臣、開府儀同三司、中書右丞相、上柱國，追封順寧王，諡忠烈。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizheng he was posthumously granted the title of Meritorious Minister for Pure Loyalty, Single Virtue, Correct Law, and Preservation of Greatness, Commissioner with Equal Protocol to the Three Dukes, Right Chancellor of the Central Secretariat, and Upper Pillar of the State; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Shunning with the posthumous name Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: In 1341 he was posthumously granted the title Meritorious Minister for Pure Loyalty, Single Virtue, Correct Law, and Preservation of Greatness, made Commissioner with Equal Protocol to the Three Dukes, Right Chancellor of the Central Secretariat, and Upper Pillar of the State, and enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Shunning with the posthumous name Zhonglie.

sentences.zh: 其繼室別哥倫氏，亦有至行，寡居三十年，未嘗妄言笑，身不服華綵。

translations.literal: His second wife, of the Biegolun clan, also had supreme conduct; widowed thirty years, she never spoke or laughed lightly, and her person did not wear ornate silks.
translations.idiomatic: His second wife, of the Biegolun clan, was likewise exemplary. Widowed for thirty years, she never spoke or laughed lightly and wore no ornate silks.

sentences.zh: 詔旌其門，與元配達海的斤氏並封順寧王夫人。

translations.literal: An edict honored her gate; she and the primary wife Dahaijinshi were together enfeoffed as Ladies of the Prince of Shunning.
translations.idiomatic: An edict honored her household, and she and his primary wife Dahaijinshi were together enfeoffed as Ladies of the Prince of Shunning.

sentences.zh: 子伯嘉訥，廉直剛敏，憂國如憂家。

translations.literal: His son Bojianu was incorrupt, upright, firm, and keen, grieving for the state as for his own family.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bojianu was upright, firm, and quick-witted, grieving for the state as for his own household.

sentences.zh: 嘗為京尹，屯儲衛誘小民梅凍兒誣首海商一百十有六人為盜而掠其貲，獄具，械送刑部，命伯嘉訥審錄之，盡得其冤狀，白丞相釋之，還其貲。

translations.literal: Once when he was capital intendant, the Garrison Storage Guard induced the commoner Mei Dong'er to falsely accuse one hundred sixteen maritime merchants as bandits and plunder their goods; the case was complete and they were sent in fetters to the Ministry of Justice; Bojianu was ordered to review and record the case, fully obtained the circumstances of their wrongful conviction, reported to the chancellor to release them, and returned their goods.
translations.idiomatic: As capital intendant, the Garrison Storage Guard induced a commoner named Mei Dong'er to accuse one hundred sixteen maritime merchants of banditry and seize their goods. When the case was sent to the Ministry of Justice in chains, Bojianu was ordered to review it, uncovered the full injustice, persuaded the chancellor to release them, and restored their property.

sentences.zh: 後遷翰林侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Hanlin Attendant Reader.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Hanlin Attendant Reader.

sentences.zh: 拜住，安童孫也。

translations.literal: Baizhu was the grandson of Antong.
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu was the grandson of Antong.

sentences.zh: 五歲而孤，太夫人教養之。

translations.literal: Orphaned at five, his lady mother raised and nurtured him.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at five, his mother raised and nurtured him.

sentences.zh: 稍長，宏遠端亮，有祖風。

translations.literal: When he grew somewhat older, he was grand, far-seeing, upright, and bright, with his grandfather's manner.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older he was grand, far-seeing, upright, and bright, with his grandfather's manner.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，襲為宿衞長。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide he inherited the post as chief of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: In 1309 he inherited the post as chief of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，延祐二年，拜資善大夫、太常禮儀院使。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, in the second year of Yanyou he was appointed as Attendant of Virtue and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong took the throne, in 1315 he was appointed Attendant of Virtue and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 四年，進榮祿大夫、大司徒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Steward.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Steward.

sentences.zh: 五年，進金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was advanced to Grand Master of the Golden Purple and Glorious Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to Grand Master of the Golden Purple and Glorious Happiness.

sentences.zh: 六年，加開府儀同三司，餘並如故。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was granted Commissioner with Equal Protocol to the Three Dukes, with all else remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was granted Commissioner with Equal Protocol to the Three Dukes, with all else remaining as before.

sentences.zh: 每議大政，必問曰：「合典故否？」

translations.literal: Whenever great affairs of government were discussed, he invariably asked, "Does this accord with precedent?"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever great affairs of government were discussed, he invariably asked, "Does this accord with precedent?"

sentences.zh: 同官有異見者，曰：「大朝止說典故耶？」

translations.literal: A colleague who held a different view said, "Does the great court speak of nothing but precedent?"
translations.idiomatic: A colleague who disagreed said, "Does the great court speak of nothing but precedent?"

sentences.zh: 拜住微笑曰：「公試言之，國朝何事不依典故？」

translations.literal: Baizhu smiled and said, "Try to say—what affair of the dynastic state does not follow precedent?"
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu smiled and said, "Try to say—what affair of the dynastic state does not follow precedent?"

sentences.zh: 同官不能對。

translations.literal: The colleague could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The colleague could not reply.

sentences.zh: 太常事簡，每退食必延儒士諮訪古今禮樂刑政、治亂得失，盡日不倦。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices had light duties; after each meal he invariably summoned Confucian scholars to consult on ancient and modern ritual, music, penal administration, political order and disorder, gains and losses, spending the whole day without tiring.
