translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices had light duties; after each meal he summoned Confucian scholars to consult on ancient and modern ritual, music, penal administration, and the gains and losses of order and disorder, spending the whole day without tiring.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「人之仕宦，隨所職司，事皆可習。

translations.literal: He once said, "In human official service, following one's office, affairs may all be learned.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "In official service, following one's office, affairs may all be learned.

sentences.zh: 至於學問有本，施於事業，此儒者之能事，宰相之資也。」

translations.literal: But as for learning with root, applied to achievement—this is what the Confucian excels at, and the chancellor's qualification."
translations.idiomatic: But learning with root, applied to achievement—this is what the Confucian excels at, and the chancellor's qualification."

sentences.zh: 英宗在東宮，問宿衛之臣於左右，咸稱拜住賢。

translations.literal: When Yingzong was in the Eastern Palace, he asked his attendants about the palace guard ministers; all praised Baizhu as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong was crown prince he asked his attendants about the palace guard ministers, and all praised Baizhu.

sentences.zh: 遣使召之，欲與語。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to summon him, wishing to converse with him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to summon Baizhu for a conversation.

sentences.zh: 拜住謂使者曰：「嫌疑之際，君子所慎，我長天子宿衛而與東宮私相往來，我固得罪，亦豈太子福耶？」

translations.literal: Baizhu told the envoys: "At a moment of suspicion the gentleman is cautious; I am chief of the Son of Heaven's palace guard yet privately associate with the Eastern Palace—I would indeed be guilty, but would that be the crown prince's blessing?"
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu told the envoys, "At a moment of suspicion a gentleman must be cautious. I command the emperor's palace guard yet would visit the crown prince privately—I would be guilty, and how would that serve the prince?"

sentences.zh: 竟不往。

translations.literal: In the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He did not go.

sentences.zh: 英宗登極，拜中書平章政事。

translations.literal: When Yingzong ascended the throne, Baizhu was appointed Central Secretariat Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong took the throne, Baizhu was appointed Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會諸侯王于大明殿，詔進讀太祖金匱寶訓，威儀整暇，語音明暢，莫不注目竦聽。

translations.literal: He assembled the feudal princes in the Daming Hall; an edict ordered him to advance and read Taizu's golden-casket precious instructions; his bearing was composed and at ease, his voice clear and flowing; none failed to fix their gaze and listen in awe.
translations.idiomatic: He assembled the princes in the Daming Hall and was ordered to read Taizu's golden-casket instructions. His bearing was composed, his voice clear, and all listened in rapt attention.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，徽政使失烈門、要束木妻也里失八等謀為逆，帝密得其事，御穆清閣，召拜住謀之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer, Palace Domestic Service Commissioner Shiliemen, Yaosumu's wife Yelishiba, and others plotted rebellion; the emperor secretly learned of the affair, presided at the Muqing Pavilion, and summoned Baizhu to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Palace Domestic Service Commissioner Shiliemen, Yaosumu's wife Yelishiba, and others plotted rebellion. The emperor learned of it in secret, went to the Muqing Pavilion, and summoned Baizhu to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「此輩擅權亂政久矣，今猶不懲，陰結黨與，謀危社稷，宜速施天威，以正祖宗法度。」

translations.literal: He replied: "These men have long monopolized power and thrown government into disorder; if they are still not punished, they secretly form factions and plot to endanger the altars of state—Heaven's majesty should swiftly be applied to rectify the ancestors' laws and institutions."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "These men have long abused power and corrupted government. If they are not punished now, they will secretly form factions and endanger the state. Your Majesty should swiftly apply Heaven's majesty to uphold the ancestral laws."

sentences.zh: 帝動容曰；

translations.literal: The emperor was moved in countenance and said:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved and said,

sentences.zh: 「此朕志也。」

translations.literal: "This is my intent."
translations.idiomatic: "That is my intent."

sentences.zh: 命率衛士擒斬之，其黨皆伏誅。

translations.literal: He ordered him to lead guards to seize and execute them; their faction all submitted to execution.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Baizhu to lead the guards to seize and execute them, and their entire faction was put to death.

sentences.zh: 拜中書左丞相。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Chancellor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Left Chancellor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 先時，近侍傳旨以姓名赴中書銓注者六七百員，選曹為之壅滯。

translations.literal: Earlier, close attendants transmitting edicts with names sent to the Central Secretariat for appointment registration numbered six or seven hundred posts, and the selection office was clogged on their account.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, close attendants had transmitted edicts naming six or seven hundred persons for appointment through the Central Secretariat, clogging the selection office.

sentences.zh: 拜住奏閣之，注授一依選格次第，吏無容姦。

translations.literal: Baizhu memorialized to close the matter; appointments followed the selection regulations in order, and clerks had no room for deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu memorialized to close the backlog; appointments followed the selection regulations in proper order, leaving clerks no room for fraud.

sentences.zh: 刑曹事有情可矜者寬恕之，貪暴不法必不少容。

translations.literal: In penal matters, where circumstances merited compassion he showed leniency; the greedy and violent who violated law he never spared.
translations.idiomatic: In criminal cases he showed mercy where compassion was warranted, but never spared the greedy or lawless.

sentences.zh: 帝常諭左右曰：「汝輩慎之，苟陷國法，我雖曲赦，拜住不汝恕也。」

translations.literal: The emperor often instructed those about him: "You must be careful—if you fall under the state laws, though I might bend to pardon you, Baizhu will not forgive you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often warned his attendants: "Be careful—if you violate the law, I may pardon you out of favor, but Baizhu will not."

sentences.zh: 至治元年春正月，帝欲結綵樓於禁中，元夕張燈設宴。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the first year of Zhizhi, the emperor wished to build a brocade tower in the forbidden precinct and on the Lantern Festival night hang lamps and set a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1321 the emperor wished to build a festooned pavilion in the palace and hold a lantern festival banquet.

sentences.zh: 時居先帝喪，參議張養浩上疏，拜住謂當進諫，即袖其疏入奏，帝悅而止，仍賜養浩帛，以旌直言。

translations.literal: At the time they were in mourning for the former emperor; Participating Councillor Zhang Yanghao submitted a memorial; Baizhu said one ought to remonstrate and at once tucked the memorial into his sleeve and entered to memorialize; the emperor was pleased and stopped, still granting Yanghao silk to honor his straight speaking.
translations.idiomatic: The court was still in mourning for the late emperor. Participating Councillor Zhang Yanghao submitted a memorial; Baizhu said it should be presented at once, tucked the memorial into his sleeve, and entered to memorialize. The emperor was pleased and abandoned the plan, granting Yanghao silk to honor his frank counsel.

sentences.zh: 三月，從幸上都，次察罕腦兒。

translations.literal: In the third month he followed the emperor in visiting Shangdu, stopping at Chahannao'er.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he accompanied the emperor to Shangdu, stopping at Chahannao'er.

sentences.zh: 帝以行宮亨麗殿制度卑隘，欲更廣之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the traveling palace's Hengli Hall was structurally low and narrow, wished to enlarge it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to enlarge the Hengli Hall of the traveling palace, finding its layout cramped.

sentences.zh: 奏曰：「此地苦寒，入夏始種粟黍，陛下初登大寶，不求民瘼，而遽興大役以妨農務，恐失民望。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: "This place is bitterly cold; only in summer do they plant millet and broomcorn millet. Your Majesty has just ascended the great treasure; if you do not seek the people's afflictions but hastily raise a great project to obstruct agricultural work, I fear you will lose the people's hopes."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "This region is bitterly cold; grain is planted only in summer. Your Majesty has just ascended the throne. If you do not address the people's hardships but hastily launch a major project that disrupts farming, you will lose their trust."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗謂拜住曰：「朕委卿以大任者，以乃祖木華黎從太祖開拓土宇，安童相世祖克成善治也。

translations.literal: The emperor once said to Baizhu: "The reason I entrust you with a great charge is that your ancestor Muqali followed Taizu in opening and expanding the realm, and Antong assisted Shizu in completing good governance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told Baizhu: "I entrust you with great responsibility because your ancestor Muqali helped Taizu conquer the realm, and Antong helped Kublai complete his good governance.

sentences.zh: 卿念祖宗令聞，豈有不盡心者乎。」

translations.literal: If you think of your ancestors' fine reputation, how could you not give your utmost?"
translations.idiomatic: Surely you will give your utmost, mindful of your ancestors' fine reputation."

sentences.zh: 拜住再拜曰：「陛下委臣以大任，臣有所畏者三：畏辱祖宗；

translations.literal: Baizhu bowed twice and said: "Your Majesty has entrusted your subject with a great charge; your subject has three things he fears: fearing to disgrace his ancestors;
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu bowed twice and said, "Your Majesty has entrusted me with great responsibility. I have three fears: fear of disgracing my ancestors;

sentences.zh: 畏天下事大，識見有所未盡；

translations.literal: fearing that the affairs of the realm are great and his understanding is not complete;
translations.idiomatic: fear that the realm's affairs are vast and my understanding incomplete;

sentences.zh: 畏年少不克負荷，無以上報聖恩。

translations.literal: fearing that in youth he cannot bear the burden and has no way to repay the sage grace.
translations.idiomatic: fear that in my youth I cannot bear the burden and have no way to repay Your Majesty's grace.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下垂閔，時加訓飭，幸甚。」

translations.literal: Only that Your Majesty show compassion and from time to time instruct and admonish—that would be most fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: I beg only that Your Majesty show compassion and instruct me from time to time—that would be my greatest fortune."

sentences.zh: 延祐間，朔漠大風雪，羊馬駝畜盡死，人民流散，以子女鬻人為奴婢。

translations.literal: During Yanyou, in the northern deserts great wind and snow struck; sheep, horses, and camels all died; the people scattered in flight, selling sons and daughters as slaves and bondmaids.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yanyou era a great blizzard struck the northern steppe; sheep, horses, and camels perished, the people scattered, and many sold their children into slavery.

sentences.zh: 拜住以興王根本之地，其民宜加賑卹，請立宗仁衛緫之，命縣官贖置衛中，以遂生養。

translations.literal: Baizhu, because this was the fundamental land where the dynasty rose, said its people ought to receive added relief; he requested establishing the Zongren Guard to oversee them, ordering district officials to redeem and place them in the guard so they might live and be nourished.
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu, seeing this as the dynasty's foundational homeland, petitioned for additional relief, proposed establishing the Zongren Guard to oversee the people, and ordered local officials to redeem those sold and settle them for livelihood.

sentences.zh: 至元十四年，始建太廟于大都，至是四十年，親享之禮未暇講肄。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan the Imperial Ancestral Temple was first built in Dadu; by now forty years had passed, yet the rites of personal sacrifice had not been studied and practiced in leisure.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Ancestral Temple had been built in Dadu in 1277; forty years later the rites of personal sacrifice had still not been properly practiced.

sentences.zh: 拜住奏曰：「古云禮樂百年而後興，郊廟祭享此其時矣。」

translations.literal: Baizhu memorialized: "The ancients said ritual and music flourish after a hundred years—sacrificial offerings at the suburban altars and temple are timely now."
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu memorialized: "The ancients said ritual and music flourish after a century—the time has come for temple sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 帝悅曰：「朕能行之。」

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and said: "I can carry this out."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and said, "I shall do it."

sentences.zh: 預敕有司，以親享太室儀注禮節，一遵典故，毋擅增損。

translations.literal: He beforehand commanded the responsible offices that for the rites and protocols of personally sacrificing at the Grand Chamber, all were to follow ancient precedents without unauthorized additions or reductions.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered officials in advance that the rites for personal sacrifice at the Grand Chamber follow ancient precedent without unauthorized change.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，始有事于太廟。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter they first performed the rites at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the emperor first performed rites at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月，孟享，始備法駕，設黃麾大仗，帝服通天冠、絳紗袍，出自崇天門。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the second year, at the seasonal offering, they first prepared the full imperial equipage, set the yellow banner great guard, the emperor wearing the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe, issuing from the Chongtian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year, at the seasonal offering, the full imperial procession was prepared with yellow banners and great guard. The emperor wore the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe and issued from the Chongtian Gate.

sentences.zh: 拜住攝太尉以從。

translations.literal: Baizhu acted as Grand Commandant in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu attended as acting Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 帝見羽衛文物之美，顧拜住曰：「朕用卿言舉行大禮，亦卿所共喜也。」

translations.literal: The emperor, seeing the beauty of the guard of honor and ritual objects, turned to Baizhu and said: "I carried out the great rite on your advice—this is what you too rejoice in."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the splendor of the guard and ritual regalia, the emperor turned to Baizhu and said, "I held this great ceremony on your advice—you must rejoice in it as well."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下以帝王之道化成天下，非獨臣之幸，實四海蒼生所共慶也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty, with the way of emperors and kings transforming and completing the realm, is not only your subject's fortune—it is truly what the myriad people under Heaven jointly celebrate."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your Majesty governs the realm by the way of sage kings. That is not my fortune alone—it is the joy of all under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 致齋大次，行酌獻禮，升降周旋，儼若素習，中外肅然。

translations.literal: After fasting in the great lodge, they performed the libation and offering rite; ascending and descending, moving about, he was as if long practiced; within and without were solemn.
translations.idiomatic: After fasting in the great lodge he performed the libation and offering rites with the ease of long practice; court and realm were solemn.

sentences.zh: 明日還宮，鼓吹交作，萬姓聳觀，百年廢典一旦復見，有感泣者。

translations.literal: The next day returning to the palace, drums and music sounded together; the myriad people looked up in awe; a hundred-year abandoned ritual was seen again in a single day; some were moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he returned to the palace amid drums and music. The people looked on in awe; a ritual abandoned for a century was restored in a day, and some wept.

sentences.zh: 拜住率百僚稱賀于大明殿，執事之臣賜金帛有差。

translations.literal: Baizhu led the hundred officials in congratulation at the Daming Hall; ministers who performed duties were granted gold and silk in differing amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu led the officials in congratulation at the Daming Hall; those who had performed the rites received gold and silk in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 又奏建太廟前殿，議行祫禘配享等禮。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to build the front hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and deliberated carrying out the rites of collective and seasonal offerings and associated sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized to build the front hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and to institute the collective and seasonal offering rites.

sentences.zh: 帝從容謂拜住曰：「朕思天下之大，非朕一人思慮所及，汝為朕股肱，毋忘規諫，以輔朕之不逮。」

translations.literal: The emperor calmly said to Baizhu: "I reflect that the realm is vast—not within the reach of my thought alone; you are my arms and legs; do not forget to remonstrate and aid where I fall short."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said calmly to Baizhu: "The realm is vast—beyond one man's thought. You are my right hand; do not forget to remonstrate and correct my shortcomings."

sentences.zh: 拜住頓首謝曰：「昔堯、舜為君，每事詢衆，善則舍己從人，萬世稱聖。

translations.literal: Baizhu bowed his head in thanks and said: "Formerly Yao and Shun as rulers on every matter consulted the multitude; when good, they set aside themselves and followed others—ten thousand generations call them sage.
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu kowtowed and said, "Yao and Shun consulted others on every matter and followed good counsel—they are called sage for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 桀、紂為君，拒諫自賢，悅人從己，好近小人，國滅而身不保，民到于今稱為無道之主。

translations.literal: Jie and Zhou as rulers rejected remonstrance and considered themselves worthy, delighted when others followed them, loved drawing near petty men—the state perished and their persons were not preserved; the people to this day call them rulers without the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Jie and Zhou rejected remonstrance, thought themselves wise, loved flatterers and petty men—their states perished and they are called tyrants to this day.

sentences.zh: 臣等仰荷洪恩，敢不竭忠以報。

translations.literal: Your subjects and I, bearing great grace, dare not fail to exhaust loyalty in repayment.
translations.idiomatic: We who bear Your Majesty's grace dare not fail to repay it with full loyalty.

sentences.zh: 然事言之則易，行之則難。

translations.literal: Yet in affairs, to speak of them is easy; to carry them out is hard.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in government, words are easy and deeds are hard.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下力行，臣等不言，則臣之罪也。」

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty forcefully acts, and your subjects do not speak—then it is your subjects' crime."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not act and we do not speak, the fault is ours."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted his words.

sentences.zh: 時右丞相鐵木迭兒貪濫譎險，屢殺大臣，鬻獄賣官，廣立朋黨，凡不附己者必以事去之，尤惡平章王毅、右丞高昉，因在京諸倉糧儲失陷，欲奏誅之。

translations.literal: At the time Right Chancellor Temuder was greedy, excessive, treacherous, and dangerous; he repeatedly killed great ministers, sold judgments and offices, broadly established factions; whoever did not attach to him he inevitably removed on some pretext; he especially hated Grand Councillor Wang Yi and Right Vice Chancellor Gao Fang; because grain stores in the capital had losses, he wished to memorialize to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Right Chancellor Temuder was greedy, treacherous, and dangerous. He repeatedly killed senior ministers, sold offices and judgments, and built factions; he especially hated Grand Councillor Wang Yi and Right Vice Chancellor Gao Fang and sought their execution over grain-store losses in the capital.

sentences.zh: 拜住密言於帝曰：「論道經邦，宰相事也，以金穀細務責之可乎？」

translations.literal: Baizhu secretly told the emperor: "Discussing the Way and ordering the state are a chancellor's affairs—is it fitting to hold them responsible for minute grain and cash matters?"
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu secretly told the emperor, "Ordering the state is a chancellor's work—is it right to blame them for grain accounts?"

sentences.zh: 帝然之，俱得不死。

translations.literal: The emperor approved; both escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and both were spared.

sentences.zh: 鐵木迭兒復引參知政事張思明為左丞以助己。

translations.literal: Temuder again brought in Associate Administrator Zhang Siming as left vice chancellor to aid himself.
translations.idiomatic: Temuder then brought in Associate Administrator Zhang Siming as Left Vice Chancellor to support him.

sentences.zh: 思明為盡力，忌拜住方正，每與其黨密語，謀中害之。

translations.literal: Siming exerted himself to the utmost, resented Baizhu's uprightness, and often with his faction spoke secretly, plotting to harm him midway.
translations.idiomatic: Siming worked zealously for him, resented Baizhu's integrity, and conspired with his faction to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 左右得其情，乘間以告，且請備之。

translations.literal: Those at left and right learned the situation, seized an interval to report it, and also asked to take precautions.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants learned of the plot, reported it when they could, and urged precautions.

sentences.zh: 拜住曰：「我祖宗為國元勳，世篤忠貞，百有餘年。

translations.literal: Baizhu said: "My ancestors were founding meritorious ministers of the state; generation after generation they were deeply loyal for more than a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu said, "My ancestors were founding meritorious ministers, loyal for more than a hundred years.

sentences.zh: 我今年少，叨受寵命，蓋以此耳。

translations.literal: I am young and have presumptuously received favor—it is for this alone.
translations.idiomatic: I am young and have received favor only because of that.

sentences.zh: 大臣協和，國之利也。

translations.literal: Harmony among great ministers is the state's advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Harmony among ministers benefits the state.

sentences.zh: 今以右相讎我，我求報之，非特吾二人之不幸，亦國家之不幸。

translations.literal: Now if the right chancellor bears me enmity and I seek to repay it, it is not only misfortune for us two—it is also the state's misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: If the right chancellor hates me and I retaliate, that harms not only us two but the state itself.

sentences.zh: 吾知盡吾心，上不負君父，下不負士民而已。

translations.literal: I know only to exhaust my heart, above not failing ruler and father, below not failing scholars and people.
translations.idiomatic: I need only do my utmost, loyal above to my sovereign and below to the people.

sentences.zh: 死生禍福，天實鑒之，汝輩毋復言。」

translations.literal: Life, death, fortune, and calamity—Heaven truly observes; you must speak no more of this."
translations.idiomatic: Life and death are in Heaven's hands—speak no more of this."

sentences.zh: 未幾，奉旨往立忠憲王碑于范陽。

translations.literal: Before long, by imperial order he went to erect the Stele of the Loyal and Worthy Prince at Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to erect the Stele of the Loyal and Worthy Prince at Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 鐵木迭兒久稱疾，聞拜住行，將出蒞省事，入朝，至內門，帝遣速速賜之酒，且曰：「卿年老宜自愛，待新年入朝未晚。」

translations.literal: Temuder had long claimed illness; hearing Baizhu was departing, he was about to go out to preside over secretariat affairs and enter court; reaching the inner gate, the emperor sent Susu to grant him wine and said: "You are aged and should cherish yourself; wait until the new year to enter court—it is not late."
translations.idiomatic: Temuder had long feigned illness. When he heard Baizhu was leaving, he prepared to resume secretariat duties and enter court. At the inner gate the emperor sent Susu with wine and said, "You are old—take care of yourself. Wait until the new year to attend court."

sentences.zh: 遂怏怏而還。

translations.literal: He then returned displeased.
translations.idiomatic: He returned displeased.

sentences.zh: 然其黨猶布列朝中，事必稟于其家，以拜住故不得大肆其奸，百計傾之，終不能遂。

translations.literal: Yet his faction still filled the court; affairs had to be reported to his household; because of Baizhu they could not greatly unleash their wickedness; they schemed in a hundred ways to overturn him but in the end could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: His faction still filled the court and routed affairs through his household. Because of Baizhu they could not fully unleash their corruption; they schemed endlessly against him but never succeeded.

sentences.zh: 在京倉漕管庫之職，歲終例應注代。

translations.literal: The duties of managing granaries, transport, and storehouses in the capital, at year's end were by rule to be registered for replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Capital posts managing granaries, transport, and storehouses were by rule rotated at year's end.

sentences.zh: 時張思明亦稱疾不出，衆皆顧望。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Siming also claimed illness and did not go out; the multitude all looked about in hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Siming also claimed illness and stayed away; officials hesitated.

sentences.zh: 拜住雖朝夕帝前，以事不可緩，乃日坐省中謂僚屬曰：「左丞病，省事遂廢乎？」

translations.literal: Though Baizhu morning and evening was before the emperor, because the matter could not be delayed he daily sat in the secretariat and told his subordinates: "The left vice chancellor is ill—is secretariat business to be abandoned?"
translations.idiomatic: Though Baizhu attended the emperor daily, the matter could not wait. He sat daily in the secretariat and told his staff, "The left vice chancellor is ill—shall government stop?"

sentences.zh: 郎中李處恭曰：「金穀之職，須慎選擇，不得其人，未敢遽擬。」

translations.literal: Director Li Chugong said: "Grain and cash duties require careful selection; without the right men I dare not hastily propose."
translations.idiomatic: Director Li Chugong said, "These grain posts require careful selection; without suitable men I dare not propose names."

sentences.zh: 拜住曰：「汝為賣官之計耳。」

translations.literal: Baizhu said: "You are making a plan to sell offices."
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu said, "You are plotting to sell offices."

sentences.zh: 遣人善慰思明，乃出共畢銓事。

translations.literal: He sent someone to console Siming kindly; Siming then came out and together they completed the selection business.
translations.idiomatic: He sent someone to urge Siming kindly; Siming then came out and they completed the appointments together.

sentences.zh: 拜住每以學校政化大源，似緩實急，而主者不務盡心，遂致廢弛，請令內外官議拯治之。

translations.literal: Baizhu often said that schools were the great source of government and transformation—seemingly slow yet actually urgent—yet those in charge did not strive to give their hearts, and thus they fell into neglect; he requested ordering inner and outer officials to deliberate saving and restoring them.
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu often said schools were the great source of governance—seemingly slow yet urgent—yet overseers neglected them. He requested that officials everywhere deliberate on their restoration.

sentences.zh: 有言佛教可治天下者，帝問之，對曰：「清淨寂滅，自治可也。

translations.literal: When someone said Buddhism could govern the realm, the emperor asked him; he replied: "Purity, stillness, and extinction suffice for self-governance.
translations.idiomatic: When someone said Buddhism could govern the realm, the emperor asked Baizhu, who replied, "Its purity and stillness suffice for self-cultivation.

sentences.zh: 若治天下，捨仁義，則綱常亂矣。」

translations.literal: If one governs the realm and abandons benevolence and righteousness, then the cardinal norms are thrown into disorder."
translations.idiomatic: To govern the realm while abandoning benevolence and righteousness would throw the cardinal norms into chaos."

sentences.zh: 又嘗謂拜住曰：「今亦有如唐魏征之敢諫者乎？」

translations.literal: He also once asked Baizhu: "Are there now any like Tang's Wei Zheng who dare remonstrate?"
translations.idiomatic: He also asked Baizhu, "Are there now men like Tang's Wei Zheng who dare remonstrate?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「槃圓則水圓，盂方則水方。

translations.literal: He replied: "When the tray is round the water is round; when the vessel is square the water is square.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "When the tray is round the water is round; when the vessel is square the water is square.

sentences.zh: 有太宗納諫之君，則有魏徵敢諫之臣。」

translations.literal: When there is a ruler like Taizong who accepts remonstrance, there will be a minister like Wei Zheng who dares remonstrate."
translations.idiomatic: When there is a ruler like Taizong who accepts remonstrance, there will be ministers like Wei Zheng who dare remonstrate."

sentences.zh: 帝並善之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all he said.

sentences.zh: 六月壬寅，敕賜平江腴田萬畝。

translations.literal: On renyin day of the sixth month an edict granted ten thousand mu of fertile fields in Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day of the sixth month an edict granted ten thousand mu of fertile land in Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 拜住辭曰：「陛下命臣釐正庶務，若先受賜田，人其謂何？」

translations.literal: Baizhu declined: "Your Majesty has ordered your subject to rectify common affairs—if I first receive granted fields, what will people say?"
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu declined: "Your Majesty has ordered me to rectify government—if I accept land first, what will people say?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「汝勳舊子孫，加以廉慎，人或援例，朕自諭之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You are the son and grandson of meritorious ministers, and moreover honest and cautious—if others cite this as precedent, I myself will instruct them."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are heir to meritorious ministers and are honest and cautious. If others cite your example, I will explain myself to them."

sentences.zh: 秋七月，奏召張思明詣上都，數其罪，杖而逐之，鐵木迭兒繼亦病卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn he memorialized to summon Zhang Siming to Shangdu, enumerated his crimes, flogged and expelled him; Temuder likewise soon died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he memorialized to summon Zhang Siming to Shangdu, listed his crimes, had him flogged and expelled; Temuder soon died as well.

sentences.zh: 拜住哭之慟。

translations.literal: Baizhu wept for him with deep grief.
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu wept for him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 初，浙民吳機以累代失業之田賣於司徒劉夔，夔賂宣政使八剌吉思買置諸寺，以益僧廩，矯詔出庫鈔六百五十萬貫酬其直。

translations.literal: Earlier, a Zhejiang commoner named Wu Ji, because of fields lost by his family for generations, sold them to Minister Liu Kui; Kui bribed Pacification Commissioner Balajisi to buy and place them in various temples to increase monks' provisions; a forged edict drew six million five hundred thousand strings from the treasury to pay the price.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a Zhejiang commoner named Wu Ji sold family fields long lost to production to Minister Liu Kui. Kui bribed Pacification Commissioner Balajisi to register the land with temples to increase monastic provisions; a forged edict drew 6.5 million strings from the treasury as payment.

sentences.zh: 田已久為他人之業，鐵木迭兒父子及鐵失等上下蒙蔽，分受之，為贓鉅萬。

translations.literal: The fields had long been others' established holdings; Temuder father and son and Tieshi and others above and below concealed it, divided and received it—the stolen goods were tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The land had long belonged to others. Temuder's faction and Tieshi concealed the fraud and divided the spoils, amounting to vast sums.

sentences.zh: 真人蔡道泰以奸殺人，獄已成，鐵木迭兒納其金，令有司變其獄。

translations.literal: The Perfected Master Cai Daitai murdered someone in adultery; the case was complete; Temuder accepted his gold and ordered the offices to alter the case.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist master Cai Daitai committed murder in an adultery case; when conviction was complete, Temuder took his bribe and ordered the case altered.

sentences.zh: 拜住舉奏二事。

translations.literal: Baizhu memorialized and reported both matters.
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu reported both cases to the throne.

sentences.zh: 命臺察鞫之，盡得其情，以田歸主，劉、蔡、八剌吉思等皆坐死，餘論罪有差。

translations.literal: He ordered the censorate to investigate and try them; the full circumstances were obtained; the fields were returned to the owner; Liu, Cai, Balajisi, and others were all sentenced to death; the rest were punished in differing degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate investigated, uncovered the full truth, restored the land to its owner, and executed Liu, Cai, Balajisi, and others; the rest were punished according to their crimes.

sentences.zh: 特赦鐵失。

translations.literal: Tieshi was specially pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Tieshi alone was specially pardoned.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，進右丞相、監修國史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter he was advanced to Right Chancellor and Supervisor of the Compilation of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was promoted to Right Chancellor and Supervisor of the Compilation of the National History.

sentences.zh: 帝欲爵以三公，懇辭，遂不置左相，獨任以政。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to ennoble him with the rank of the Three Dukes; he earnestly declined, and so the left chancellorship was not established; he alone was entrusted with government.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to grant him rank equal to the Three Dukes; he declined earnestly, the left chancellorship was left vacant, and he governed alone.

sentences.zh: 首薦張珪，復平章政事，召用致仕老臣，優其祿秩，議事中書。

translations.literal: He first recommended Zhang Gui, restored him as Grand Councillor, summoned retired old ministers, favored their salaries and ranks, and deliberated affairs at the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He first recommended Zhang Gui and restored him as Grand Councillor, summoned retired elders, improved their stipends, and had them deliberate at the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 不次用才，唯恐少後，日以進賢退不肖為重務。

translations.literal: He employed talent out of turn, fearing only to fall short, daily making advancing the worthy and removing the unworthy his heavy task.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed talent without regard to routine precedence, making the advancement of the worthy and removal of the unworthy his daily priority.

sentences.zh: 患法制不一有司無所守，奏詳定舊典以為通制。

translations.literal: He grieved that legal institutions were not uniform and offices had nothing to adhere to; he memorialized to examine and fix old canons as a general code.
translations.idiomatic: Lamenting inconsistent laws and offices without standards, he memorialized to codify ancient statutes as a general regulation.

sentences.zh: 帝幸五臺，拜住奏曰：「自古帝王得天下以得民心為本，失其心則失天下。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Wutai, Baizhu memorialized: "From antiquity emperors and kings who gained the realm took winning the people's hearts as fundamental; lose their hearts and they lose the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Wutai, Baizhu memorialized: "Since antiquity rulers have held the people's hearts fundamental; lose the hearts and you lose the realm.

sentences.zh: 錢穀，民之膏血，多取則民困而國危，薄斂則民足而國安。」

translations.literal: Money and grain are the people's essential blood; take much and the people are distressed and the state endangered; light levies and the people are sufficient and the state secure."
translations.idiomatic: Revenue is the people's lifeblood; heavy exaction distresses the people and endangers the state; light levies make the people secure and the state strong."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿言甚善。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words are very good.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said.

sentences.zh: 朕思之，民為重，君為輕，國非民將何以為君？

translations.literal: I reflect that the people are heavy and the ruler light—without the people, for what would the ruler exist?
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that the people are weighty and the ruler light—without the people, what is a ruler for?

sentences.zh: 今理民之事卿等當熟慮而慎行之。」

translations.literal: Now in governing the people's affairs you and others should think carefully and carry them out cautiously."
translations.idiomatic: In governing the people you must all think carefully and act with caution."

sentences.zh: 三年春二月，將進仁宗實錄，先一日，詣翰林國史院聽讀。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring of the third year, when about to present the Veritable Record of Renzong, one day beforehand he went to the Hanlin National History Academy to listen to the reading.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year, before presenting the Veritable Record of Renzong, he went a day early to the Hanlin National History Academy to hear it read.

sentences.zh: 首卷書大德十一年事，不書左丞相哈剌哈孫定策功，惟書越王禿剌勇決從容。

translations.literal: The first scroll recorded affairs of the eleventh year of Dade but did not record Left Chancellor Harqasun Darqan's merit in fixing the succession strategy; it only recorded Prince of Yue Tula's courageous decisiveness and composure.
translations.idiomatic: The first scroll recorded the eleventh year of Dade but omitted Left Chancellor Harqasun Darqan's role in securing the succession, recording only Prince of Yue Tula's courage.

sentences.zh: 謂史官曰：「無左丞相，雖百越王何益？

translations.literal: He told the historiographers: "Without the left chancellor, even a hundred Princes of Yue would be of what use?
translations.idiomatic: He told the historians, "Without the left chancellor, what good were a hundred Princes of Yue?

sentences.zh: 錄鷹犬之勞，而略發蹤指示之人，可乎？」

translations.literal: To record the falcon-hound's labor yet omit the man who showed the track—can that be done?"
translations.idiomatic: To record the hound's chase and omit the huntsman who showed the trail—can that stand?"

sentences.zh: 立命書之。

translations.literal: He at once ordered it written.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered it written at once.

sentences.zh: 其他筆削未盡善者，一一正之，人皆服其識見。

translations.literal: Other editorial cuts not yet fully good he corrected one by one; people all submitted to his discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Other editorial lapses he corrected one by one, and all respected his judgment.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，拜住以海運糧視世祖時頓增數倍，今江南民力困極，而京倉充滿，奏請歲減二十萬石。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer Baizhu, because sea-transport grain compared with Shizu's time had suddenly increased several fold while Jiangnan popular strength was extremely exhausted yet the capital granaries were full, memorialized to reduce two hundred thousand shi yearly.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Baizhu noted that sea transport had multiplied several times since Kublai's day while Jiangnan was exhausted and capital granaries full; he memorialized to cut two hundred thousand shi per year.

sentences.zh: 帝遂併鐵木迭兒所增江淮糧免之。

translations.literal: The emperor then together exempted the Jiang-Huai grain Temuder had added.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also abolished the extra Jiang-Huai levies Temuder had imposed.

sentences.zh: 時鐵木迭兒過惡日彰，拜住悉以奏聞。

translations.literal: At the time Temuder's excesses daily grew manifest; Baizhu reported them all to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: As Temuder's crimes grew ever clearer, Baizhu reported them all.

sentences.zh: 帝悟，奪其官，仆其碑。

translations.literal: The emperor understood, stripped his offices, and toppled his stele.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood, stripped his offices, and toppled his memorial stele.

sentences.zh: 奸黨鐵失等甚懼。

translations.literal: The wicked faction of Tieshi and others were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The conspirators led by Tieshi were terrified.

sentences.zh: 帝在上都，夜寐不寧，命作佛事。

translations.literal: The emperor was at Shangdu; at night his sleep was unquiet; he ordered Buddhist rites performed.
translations.idiomatic: At Shangdu the emperor slept poorly and ordered Buddhist rites.

sentences.zh: 拜住以國用不足諫止之。

translations.literal: Baizhu, because state expenditures were insufficient, remonstrated and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu remonstrated that state funds were insufficient and stopped it.

sentences.zh: 既而懼誅者復陰誘群僧言：「國當有厄，非作佛事而大赦無以禳之。」

translations.literal: Before long those who feared execution again secretly induced the monks to say: "The state will suffer calamity; unless Buddhist rites are performed and a great amnesty proclaimed, it cannot be averted."
translations.idiomatic: Soon those fearing punishment secretly urged monks to say, "The realm faces calamity; only grand Buddhist rites and a great amnesty can avert it."

sentences.zh: 拜住叱曰：「爾輩不過圖得金帛而已，又欲庇有罪耶？」

translations.literal: Baizhu rebuked them: "You people seek nothing but to obtain gold and silk—and also wish to shelter the guilty?"
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu rebuked them, "You seek only gold and silk—and wish to shelter criminals besides?"

sentences.zh: 奸黨聞之益懼，乃生異謀。

translations.literal: The wicked faction, hearing this, feared all the more and then hatched a different plot.
translations.idiomatic: The conspirators grew still more afraid and plotted anew.

sentences.zh: 晉王也孫帖木兒時鎮北邊，鐵失潛遣人至王所，告以逆謀，約事成推王為帝。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Yesun Temur at the time guarded the northern frontier; Tieshi secretly sent someone to the prince's place, informing him of the rebellious plot, agreeing that when the affair succeeded the prince would be pushed as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jin Yesun Temur was then guarding the north. Tieshi secretly sent word offering to make him emperor if the plot succeeded.

sentences.zh: 王命囚之，遣使赴上都告變，未至，車駕南還，次南坡，鐵失與赤斤鐵木兒等夜以所領阿速衛兵為外應，殺拜住，遂弒帝於行幄。

translations.literal: The prince ordered him imprisoned and sent envoys to Shangdu to report the treason; before they arrived the imperial carriage returned south, stopping at Nanpo; Tieshi with Chijin Temur and others by night used the Asud guard troops they commanded as external support, killed Baizhu, and then assassinated the emperor in the traveling tent.
translations.idiomatic: The prince had the messenger imprisoned and sent word to Shangdu, but before it arrived the emperor was returning south and halted at Nanpo. Tieshi and Chijin Temur used Asud guards as accomplices by night, killed Baizhu, and assassinated the emperor in his tent.

sentences.zh: 晉王即位，鐵失等伏誅。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin ascended the throne; Tieshi and others were executed.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin took the throne; Tieshi and his confederates were executed.

sentences.zh: 詔有司備儀衛，百官耆宿前導，輿拜住畫相於海雲寺，大作佛事，觀者萬數，無不歎惜泣下。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the responsible offices to prepare guard of honor; hundred officials and elders led the way; they carried Baizhu's painted portrait to Haiyun Temple and performed great Buddhist rites; viewers numbered in the tens of thousands, none who did not sigh in regret and weep.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered full ceremonial honors; elders and officials led the procession bearing Baizhu's portrait to Haiyun Temple for grand Buddhist rites. Tens of thousands watched, sighing and weeping.

sentences.zh: 拜住憂國忘家，常直內庭，知無不言。

translations.literal: Baizhu grieved for the state and forgot his family, constantly attending in the inner court, speaking without reserve on whatever he knew.
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu forgot family for the state, constantly attending the inner court and speaking frankly on all he knew.

sentences.zh: 太官以酒進，則憂形于色。

translations.literal: When the Imperial Kitchen presented wine, worry showed in his countenance.
translations.idiomatic: When the Imperial Kitchen brought wine, worry showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 有盜其家金器百餘兩，他寶直鉅萬，繼而獲盜得金，家僮來告，色無喜慍。

translations.literal: Thieves stole more than a hundred taels of gold vessels from his house and other treasures worth tens of thousands; later the thief was captured and the gold recovered; household servants came to report; his expression showed neither joy nor anger.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves stole gold vessels worth more than a hundred taels and other treasures worth tens of thousands from his home; when the gold was recovered and servants reported it, his face showed neither joy nor anger.

sentences.zh: 自延祐末，水旱相仍，民不聊生。

translations.literal: From the end of Yanyou, flood and drought followed in succession; the people could not sustain life.
translations.idiomatic: From the late Yanyou era floods and droughts followed one another and the people could not live.

sentences.zh: 及拜住入相，振立紀綱，修舉廢墜，裁不急之務，杜僥倖之門，加惠兵民，輕徭薄斂。

translations.literal: When Baizhu entered the chancellorship, he raised and established discipline, restored what was abandoned and fallen, cut non-urgent affairs, blocked the gate of undeserved fortune, added favor to soldiers and people, and made corvée light and levies thin.
translations.idiomatic: When Baizhu became chancellor he restored discipline, revived neglected institutions, cut nonessential business, closed paths to undeserved favor, aided soldiers and civilians, and lightened labor and taxes.

sentences.zh: 英宗倚之，相與勵精圖治。

translations.literal: Yingzong relied on him; together they strove to refine spirit and plan good government.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong relied on him, and together they strove to govern well.

sentences.zh: 時天下晏然，國富民足，遠夷有古未通中國者皆朝貢請吏，而奸臣畏之，卒搆禍難云。

translations.literal: At the time the realm was tranquil, the state rich and the people sufficient; distant barbarians who from antiquity had not communicated with China all came to court with tribute and requested officials; yet wicked ministers feared him and in the end engineered calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The realm grew tranquil, the state prosperous and the people at ease; distant peoples never before in contact with China came to offer tribute and request officials. Wicked ministers feared him and at last brought about his destruction.

sentences.zh: 母怯烈氏，年二十二，寡居守節。

translations.literal: His mother Qielie clan, aged twenty-two, widowed and kept chastity.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, of the Qielie clan, was twenty-two when widowed and remained chaste.

sentences.zh: 初，拜住為太常禮儀院使，年方二十，吏就第請署字，適在後圃閱群戲，出稍後，母厲聲呵之曰：「官事不治，若爾所為豈大人事耶？」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Baizhu was Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, aged just twenty, clerks came to his residence requesting his signature; he happened to be in the rear garden watching group games and came out somewhat late; his mother sternly rebuked him: "You do not manage official business—is what you do the affair of a grown man?"
translations.idiomatic: When Baizhu was twenty and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, clerks came to his house for his signature while he was watching games in the rear garden. His mother rebuked him sharply: "You neglect official business—is this how a grown man behaves?"

sentences.zh: 拜住深自克責。

translations.literal: Baizhu deeply blamed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu reproached himself deeply.

sentences.zh: 一日入內侍宴，英宗素知其不飲，是日強以數卮，既歸，母戒之曰：「天子試汝量，故強汝飲。

translations.literal: One day he entered to attend a banquet; Yingzong knew he did not drink; that day he forced several cups on him; after returning, his mother admonished him: "The Son of Heaven was testing your capacity, hence he forced you to drink.
translations.idiomatic: Once, attending a banquet, Yingzong knew he did not drink yet pressed several cups on him. When he returned, his mother warned him, "The emperor was testing your capacity—that is why he pressed you to drink.

sentences.zh: 汝當日益戒懼，無酣于酒。」

translations.literal: You must daily grow more cautious and fearful—do not become drunk on wine."
translations.idiomatic: You must grow daily more cautious and never become drunk."

sentences.zh: 又常代祀睿宗原廟，歸侍左右，母問之曰：「真定官府待汝若何？」

translations.literal: He also often substituted in sacrificing at Ruizong's original temple; returning to attend by her side, his mother asked: "How did the Zhending officials treat you?"
translations.idiomatic: He often substituted at sacrifices at Ruizong's original temple. On returning to her side his mother asked, "How did the Zhending officials treat you?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「所待甚重。」

translations.literal: He replied: "They treated me very respectfully."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "With great respect."

sentences.zh: 母曰：「彼以天子威靈、汝先世勳德故耳，汝何有焉？」

translations.literal: His mother said: "They do so because of the Son of Heaven's august might and your ancestors' meritorious virtue—what do you have of your own?"
translations.idiomatic: His mother said, "They do so only because of the emperor's authority and your ancestors' merit—what is that to you?"

sentences.zh: 拜住之賢，母之教也。

translations.literal: Baizhu's worthiness was his mother's teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu's excellence came from his mother's teaching.

sentences.zh: 後封東平王夫人。

translations.literal: Later she was enfeoffed as Lady of the Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: She was later enfeoffed as Lady of the Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 泰定初，中書奏丞相拜住盡忠效節，殞于群凶，乞賜褒崇以光後世。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhiding, the Central Secretariat memorialized that Chancellor Baizhu exhausted loyalty and showed integrity, perishing at the hands of a gang of villains, and requested bestowal of praise and elevation to glorify later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhiding reign the Central Secretariat memorialized that Chancellor Baizhu had served with full loyalty and died at the hands of assassins, requesting posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 制贈清忠一德佐運功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國，追封東平王，諡忠獻。

translations.literal: An order granted the title of Meritorious Minister of Pure Loyalty and One Virtue Assisting the Mandate, Grand Preceptor, Commissioner with Equal Protocol to the Three Dukes, Supreme Pillar of State; posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping with the temple name Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the title Meritorious Minister of Pure Loyalty and One Virtue Assisting the Mandate, Grand Preceptor, Commissioner with Equal Protocol to the Three Dukes, and Supreme Pillar of State, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping with the temple name Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 至正初，改至仁孚道一德佐運功臣，餘如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhizheng it was changed to Meritorious Minister of Humaneness and Sincerity Assisting the Mandate; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhizheng the title was changed to Meritorious Minister of Humaneness and Sincerity Assisting the Mandate; other honors remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 子篤麟鐵穆爾。

translations.literal: His son was Dulintemur.
translations.idiomatic: He left a son, Dulintemur.
